+# Development Plan: tooling for agentic app creation (claude/agentic-app-creation-tools-iyhb97 branch)
+
+*Started on 2026-10-08, following the EPCC workflow (Explore, Plan, Code, Commit) of [codemcp/workflows](https://github.com/mrsimpson/responsible-vibe-mcp)*
+
+## Goal
+
+A creator builds a learning app with their AI assistant, and it comes out static, frontend-only, collecting nothing,
+accessible and ready to list on lernapps.net. This increment designs and then builds the tooling for that: how the
+agent is guided through the work, what it starts from, which conventions it follows, what it can check by itself, and
+how the result is validated before listing. It implements the platform design's service for creators, D6
+`s-building-guidance` ("Agent guidance and starter templates" in D1), tracked in
+[lernapps/.github#12](https://github.com/lernapps/.github/issues/12).
+
+The architecture is documented with arc42 ([doctoolchain/arc42-language](https://github.com/doctoolchain/arc42-language),
+the skill `arc42-language` as in lernapps/docs) before anything is built.
+
+---
+
+## Key Decisions
+
+### KD-01: Five layers support the creator's agent
+1. **Process guidance**: the agent follows a plan with phases instead of running through all steps at once.
+2. **Scaffolding**: a starting point per kind of app, with strict coding conventions and git hooks.
+3. **Conventions**: general rules and type-specific guidance, packaged as skills.
+4. **Deterministic verification**: the toolchain's lint, format, type and test checks plus our own linters and CLIs
+   for lernapps-specific rules (e.g. no requests to other servers before a click).
+5. **Formal validation**: a review run by an agent before listing. It re-uses the checks of layer 4 and spends its
+   judgment on what they cannot decide.
+
+Layers 1–4 help the creator while building; layer 5 is the platform's gate.
+
+### KD-02: The app archetype is the axis across the layers
+"Content app" (like the Mathe-Karte: pages, explanations, exercises, readable without JavaScript) and "playful app"
+(like a ten-finger typing trainer: a classic SPA) differ in more than the scaffold. An archetype is a bundle:
+scaffold + skills + check profile + review rubric. Example: the content archetype requires every page to be readable
+without JavaScript; the SPA archetype requires a static page that says what the app does and a `<noscript>`
+explanation instead.
+- **Decision**: Every building block is designed per archetype from the start, with shared parts for what all
+  archetypes have in common. The archetype is chosen in the Explore phase of the creator's plan, from the operator's
+  answers, not before the conversation starts.
+- **Open**: the final names and the exact list of archetypes; two to start with.
+
+### KD-03: Process guidance is EPCC in AGENTS.md, with a Markdown plan
+The agent writes a human-readable plan file with one section per phase (Explore, Plan, Code, Commit), tasks and key
+decisions, like this file. It works through one phase at a time and stops at the human checkpoints: the scope (what
+the app teaches or trains), the plan, publishing, listing.
+- **Decision**: The workflow is written out in the scaffold's `AGENTS.md` as plain instructions, so it works with any
+  agent and without an MCP server. `@codemcp/workflows` stays an option for creators who want it.
+- **Decision**: In the Explore phase, the agent asks the operator what the catalog needs later (see KD-04), so the
+  answers are in the plan when the app is listed.
+
+### KD-04: The entry schema explains itself; the guidance only points to it
+The entry model (`schemas/entry.js` in lernapps/apps, published as `entry.v1.schema.json`) was made in an earlier
+version and may not yet serve the main job well: finding the right app. It will be tuned.
+- **Decision**: The guidance never repeats or extends the entry's fields. It tells the agent to fetch the published
+  schema and fill it in. Everything the agent needs to know about a field is in the schema's descriptions, so the
+  schema has to be self-explanatory.
+- **Consequence**: Tuning the entry model for discovery is work in lernapps/apps, outside this increment; the tooling
+  keeps working because it only refers to the schema.
+
+### KD-05: A generator with versioned packages instead of one template repo
+A GitHub template repo is chosen before the conversation and copied once, then it drifts. With several archetypes it
+also cannot be the single starting point.
+- **Decision**: The scaffold is generated for the archetype chosen in the plan. The generated app holds thin files
+  that refer to versioned packages (toolchain config, our lint rules and CLIs, the site frame), installed from git and
+  kept current by Renovate, as `@lernapps/site` and the site actions already are.
+- **Open**: what becomes of lernapps/app-template (archetype templates, the generator itself, or the starting point
+  for the first archetype); how the generator is invoked (`vp create` with our templates or `npm create`).
+
+### KD-06: vite-plus is the default toolchain, configured by the archetype
+[Vite+](https://viteplus.dev/) (`vp`) chains lint (Oxlint), format (Oxfmt), type check, test (Vitest) and the
+pre-commit run on staged files (`vp staged`, hooks installed with `vp config`) behind one CLI and one config file.
+- **Decision**: Scaffolds use vite-plus with its defaults, made stricter where our conventions need it. The config is
+  owned by the archetype package, not written by each app. The content archetype may build with Eleventy and use `vp`
+  for lint, format, test and staged only. i18n and accessibility are part of the scaffolds.
+- **Risk**: vite-plus is before 1.0 and its config format may still change; owning the config centrally keeps a
+  change in one place.
+
+### KD-07: Git hooks enforce, agent hooks are extra
+Creators use different agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, claude.ai without a shell).
+- **Decision**: Enforcement lives in git hooks, which are agent-neutral: the fast checks on pre-commit (`vp staged`),
+  the slower ones (build, our CLIs, browser checks) on pre-push. Agent-specific hooks may add the same checks earlier
+  but never replace them.
+
+### KD-08: Conventions are skills, general and type-specific
+- **Decision**: Rules are split into general rules for every app (privacy, accessibility, language, licensing,
+  "rules that came from mistakes") and type-specific guidance: per archetype, and per topic, e.g. using third-party
+  content in content-heavy apps (bundle it instead of fetching it, name source and license next to it), videos, curriculum
+  references. Packaged as skills in the agentskills.io format, distributed from this repo (e.g. `npx skills add`, a
+  Claude Code plugin marketplace).
+- **Source**: the `lern-app` skill of the Mathe-Karte (`werkzeuge/skill/lern-app/`), generalised and freed of its
+  monorepo layout.
+
+### KD-09: Our own checks run outside our scaffolds too
+- **Decision**: The lernapps-specific checks are a standalone CLI (and lint rules where a rule fits a linter), so they
+  run in our scaffolds, in apps built otherwise (the Mathe-Karte builds with Eleventy) and in the formal validation.
+  Error messages are written for an agent: what failed, where, how to fix it.
+- **Scope**: no requests to other servers before a click, what is stored (cookies, local storage, IndexedDB,
+  requests that send data), readable without JavaScript where the archetype requires it, 360 px without overflow,
+  axe, links and legal links (today `lernapps-check` in the site frame), a dependency policy (license allowlist,
+  audit, no runtime CDN).
+- **Source**: `e2e/` (`extern`, `ohne-js`, `ueberlauf`, `axe`) and `lib/pruefe-*.js` of the Mathe-Karte,
+  `lernapps-check` in lernapps.github.io.
+
+### KD-10: Formal validation is an agent review that starts from the deterministic checks
+- **Decision**: A review agent in a fresh context validates an app before listing. It runs the checks of KD-09
+  first, then focuses on what they cannot decide: the built bundle and external dependencies, whether learners act
+  themselves, ads, plain German, learner-specific data in public texts, the archetype's rubric. It works on a
+  deployed URL or a built bundle alone, so it also covers apps not built with our tooling.
+- **Decision**: The result is a report bound to the commit it reviewed. Its deterministic part provides the entry's
+  `fitness` values, so they are measured, not self-declared.
+- **Source**: `werkzeuge/review/ki-review.md` of the Mathe-Karte (verdict per head commit).
+
+### KD-11: Content correctness is suggested, never a prerequisite
+Whether content is correct can only be checked reliably where answers are computable: maths, partly the natural
+sciences.
+- **Decision**: The guidance suggests ways to support correctness (generator and checker tests for exercises, cited
+  curriculum sources, verified video and article links, a content-error issue form in the scaffold). None of it is a
+  condition for validation or listing.
+
+### KD-12: Findings move down the layers
+- **Decision**: A finding of the formal validation that recurs becomes a deterministic check (layer 4) where
+  possible, otherwise a convention (layer 3); what is forgotten again and again becomes a step or a question in the
+  process guidance (layer 1). Review findings name the layer they should move to. This is how the guidance improves,
+  in the spirit of the learning engine (D6).
+
+### KD-13: Apps live anywhere; the catalog entry is a fact sheet with a link (later)
+Apps are meant to be deployed outside lernapps.net's GitHub Pages as well.
+- **Decision**: A catalog entry renders a fact sheet of the app and links to where it is deployed. A mechanism has to
+  make sure the deployed app comes from the same commit the entry (and its validation) refers to.
+- **Deferred**: implemented in a later increment. This increment keeps the validation report bound to a commit
+  (KD-10), so the mechanism can build on it.
+
+### KD-14: The guidance itself is tested (evals)
+- **Decision**: A small set of creator prompts, at least one per archetype, is run against the scaffolds and skills
+  and scored with the checks and the review. This catches regressions when guidance changes and measures the MVP
+  assumption `a-creators-list` ("creators list an app when it costs minutes"): time from the first prompt to an entry
+  ready to list.
+
+### KD-15: Re-validation of listed apps (later)
+Apps change after they are listed; a validation does not stay true by itself.
+- **Deferred**: listed apps are re-validated on a schedule and when they change, in lernapps/apps.
+
+## Notes
+
+- **Existing building blocks**: site actions and Renovate preset (this repo); site frame with `lernapps-check`
+  (lernapps.github.io `site-frame/`); entry schema, `llms.txt` listing guide and listing criteria (lernapps/apps,
+  `schemas/entry.js`, `src/llms.njk`, `src/_data/de.js` `list.criteria`).
+- **From the Mathe-Karte** (lernapps/mathe-karte): `werkzeuge/skill/lern-app/` (skill and sub-agent brief),
+  `werkzeuge/review/ki-review.md`, `e2e/` (Playwright + axe), `lib/pruefe-ausgabe.js`, `lib/pruefe-links.js`,
+  `lib/pruefe-lizenzen.js`, `CLAUDE.md` (project rules).
+- **Org rules every app must meet** (ORGANIZATION.md): no cookies, no tracking, no requests to other servers before
+  a click; readable without JavaScript, WCAG 2.1 AA, usable at 360 px; imprint and privacy notice linked. Shared
+  infrastructure in English, texts for learners, teachers and parents in German.
+- **Language of this plan**: English, as all shared infrastructure.
+- **Issue #12** asked for a single app-template with `AGENTS.md`, the site frame and the site actions. KD-02 and
+  KD-05 widen that to archetypes and a generator; update the issue once the architecture is agreed.
+
+## Explore
+
+### Tasks
+
+### Completed
+- [x] Read the platform design for creators (D1, D6 `s-building-guidance`, D8 `a-creators-list`,
+  `a-creators-unpaid`) and issue lernapps/.github#12
+- [x] Survey existing building blocks in tooling, lernapps.github.io (site frame), apps (entry schema, listing guide),
+  app-template (empty)
+- [x] Survey the Mathe-Karte's skill, review prompt, browser tests and checks as the source to generalise
+- [x] Look at codemcp/workflows (EPCC, plan file) and vite-plus (`vp check`, `vp staged`, `vp config`)
+- [x] Agree on the five layers and the missing aspects with the owner (KD-01 – KD-15)
+
+## Plan
+
+### Tasks
+- [ ] Set up arc42 in this repo with the skill `arc42-language` (doctoolchain/arc42-language), following
+  `arc42 guide chapter <n>` per chapter
+- [ ] Ch. 1 Introduction and goals: the creator's job, quality goals (agent reaches a listable app in few iterations,
+  no hidden data collection, works with any agent, guidance stays current)
+- [ ] Ch. 2 Constraints: org rules, GitHub as means of production, frontend-only, MIT, English infrastructure
+- [ ] Ch. 3 Context: creator, creator's agent, operator answers, lernapps/apps (catalog), hosting, review agent
+- [ ] Ch. 4 Solution strategy: five layers × archetypes (KD-01, KD-02), promotion path (KD-12)
+- [ ] Ch. 5 Building blocks: process guidance, generator and archetype packages, skills, check CLI and lint rules,
+  formal validation, evals; which repo holds what (tooling, app-template, apps)
+- [ ] Ch. 6 Runtime: a creator from first prompt to listing; validation of a listing PR
+- [ ] Ch. 7 Deployment: distribution from git with Renovate; hosting on lernapps.net or elsewhere (KD-13)
+- [ ] Ch. 8 Cross-cutting concepts: plan file, human checkpoints, error messages for agents, i18n, a11y, third-party
+  content
+- [ ] Ch. 9 Decisions: carry KD-03 – KD-13 over as ADRs where they are architecture decisions
+- [ ] Ch. 10 – 11 Quality scenarios and risks (vite-plus before 1.0, agents skipping phases, schema drift)
+- [ ] Settle the open points of KD-02 and KD-05 with the owner
+- [ ] Order of building for the Code phase, smallest useful slice first
+
+### Completed
+
+## Code
+
+### Tasks
+*To be filled from the architecture (Plan phase). Expected building blocks, order to be decided:*
+- [ ] Check CLI and lint rules (KD-09)
+- [ ] Archetype packages with vite-plus config and git hooks (KD-05 – KD-07)
+- [ ] Generator and the first archetype scaffold with `AGENTS.md` (KD-03, KD-05)
+- [ ] Skills: general rules, per archetype, third-party content (KD-08)
+- [ ] Formal validation: review prompt and report (KD-10)
+- [ ] Evals (KD-14)
+
+### Completed
+
+## Commit
+
+### Tasks
+- [ ] Update the READMEs of tooling and app-template and ORGANIZATION.md "Where to find what"
+- [ ] Update lernapps/.github#12 to the agreed scope
+- [ ] Pull request per repo, previews green
+
+### Completed

thirteen scenarios, each naming where its number comes from (evals,

+### KD-16: Quality goals are grounded in the platform design; metrics name their source
+Seven goals, each traced to the platform design: simple to build with guidance (`x-list-and-hear-back`), list in
+minutes (`ch-listing`, `a-creators-list`), checked not declared (`ch-fitness-signal`), nothing collected in secret,
+also by the tooling (KD-18, `ch-feedback`); with medium priority fewer iterations for the assistant
+(`e-ai-assistants`), works through any assistant, the guidance evolves (`s-contribute-practices`).
+- **Decision**: Simplicity (creator) and cost (assistant's iterations) stay separate goals.
+- **Decision**: Other people's assistants cannot be observed, and nothing is collected in secret. Metrics are

author: Claude
message:
feat(tooling): package @lernapps/tooling with the CLI lernapps, vite-plus, hooks and check in CI

## Intent
The tooling is built with the conventions it gives apps before anything is built on it (#10): one package
installed from git, strict TypeScript, vite-plus as the toolchain, git hooks that enforce, and CI that runs
exactly what the hooks run.

## Key decisions
- The repo root is the package @lernapps/tooling: bin `lernapps` built into dist/ by `prepare` (`vp pack`),
  so an install from git works; Node does not strip types under node_modules. In this repo the scripts run
  src/cli.ts directly with Node's type stripping. `exports` holds only ./package.json for now.
- `lernapps check`: `--pre-commit` runs `vp check` (format, lint, type check), `--pre-push` runs `vp test`
  and `vp pack`; no flag or both flags run both. Parsing with node:util parseArgs, no dependency.
- Hooks with vite-plus (`vp config` in `prepare`, scripts in .vite-hooks/): pre-commit runs `vp staged`
  (format and fix the staged files) and `lernapps check --pre-commit`; pre-push `lernapps check --pre-push`.
- New workflow check.yml, job `check`: `npm run lernapps -- check`, the two hook parts together.
- `npm run check` keeps the contract of the site actions: the code checks, then the docs build and
  `lernapps-check --site /tooling/`, so a fresh clone is green with `npm ci && npm run check`.
- Strict tsconfig (strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes, noImplicitOverride and
  more); lint forbids `any`; a test forbids JavaScript sources. scripts/review-summary.mjs migrated to
  TypeScript, run by Node's type stripping, output unchanged.
- Tests first, from the consumer's contract, end to end: a fresh clone with a real `npm ci`; a planted type
  error, lint error or failing test turns the hook commands, git commit / git push and the CI command red;
  an install from git provides `lernapps`; usage and exit codes of the CLI. No unit tests of internals.
- vite-plus 1.0.0 pinned exactly (1.1.0 is younger than the preset's minimum release age); `vite` is
  overridden with @voidzero-dev/vite-plus-core as its README asks, without it npm cannot install it.

## Side effects (if any)
- `npm ci` now also builds dist/ and sets core.hooksPath to .vite-hooks/_ in the clone.
- The Pages and preview jobs run the code checks too, as part of `npm run check`, and build the docs twice.
- pr-preview.yml runs scripts/review-summary.ts.

author: Claude
message:
fix(check): npm run check builds nothing; the Pages job becomes `site`

## Intent
`npm run check` checks the code and nothing else: running a build inside a check was unexpected. The job of
pages.yml that builds and checks the docs site was also named `check`, next to the code check of check.yml;
it is renamed after what it does.

## Key decisions
- Scripts: `check` runs `lernapps check` (format, lint, types, tests, package build of the CLI) and builds no
  site; `check:site` runs `lernapps-check` on the built docs; `build` stays the docs build.
- The site actions `site-check` and `site-preview` get an input `check-script` (default `check`), so a repo whose
  `check` checks its code names its site check. Backward compatible for every other site.
- pages.yml: job `check` becomes `site` (build and check of the docs site, upload on main); `deploy` needs
  `site`. pages.yml and pr-preview.yml use the site actions from the checkout instead of a pinned commit, so
  a change to an action is exercised by its own pull request (open point of #6).
- Tests: `npm run check` on a fresh clone leaves no `_site/`; `npm run build && npm run check:site` is green.

## Side effects (if any)
- The required status `check` is now satisfied by check.yml only; the docs site job reports as `site`. Branch
  protection may want `site` added as a required check.
- Other site repos keep their job `check`; the default of `check-script` changes nothing for them.

message:
feat(guidance): AGENTS.md, the plan template, its front matter schema and the skill lernapps-app

## Intent
The EPCC workflow as plain text for any assistant (#14): a short AGENTS.md that makes the assistant keep a
plan, follow its phases, stop at the creator's checkpoints and load the skills; a plan template whose
comments guide the assistant through Explore, Plan, Code and Commit and end in a retrospective; the skill

- Front matter schema as JSON Schema (plan-front-matter.v1.schema.json), versioned in its name: archetype
  (explainer, interactive, quiz, or null until chosen), phase (explore, plan, code, commit) and
  prePushFailures (integer >= 0, written only by the hook). From phase plan on, archetype must be set.
  Additional keys are rejected so a misspelt counter is caught.

  needs to help adults find the app and keeps an entry draft in the plan.
- Checkpoints are marked "**Checkpoint:**" in the task lists: confirm the plan, publish, list.
- The retrospective has fixed headings (phases reached, failed checks, creator turns after the plan, where
  I had to guess); the review and evals read them.
- AGENTS.md points to the template in node_modules and, before the app exists, to its raw URL on main.

  the ids are meant to stay.

message:
fix(test): keep the hook's git variables out of the tests' temporary repos

## Intent
Run from the pre-push hook of a worktree, the end-to-end tests inherited GIT_DIR and GIT_INDEX_FILE from git.
Their `git init`, `git add` and `git commit` in temporary directories then acted on the repo being pushed:
the fresh clone had "nothing to commit", the push failed, and `git init` rewrote the shared config.

## Key decisions
- testEnv drops every inherited GIT_* variable, then sets the test identity as before. Every command the
  tests start runs in its own directory and needs none of them.
- Checked with GIT_DIR and GIT_INDEX_FILE pointing nowhere: the whole suite passes.

## Side effects (if any)
None for CI, which runs no hooks.

* feat(rules): rule blocks, the id test, the first listing and site rules, the rule page

## Intent
Make the rules that live in their artifacts one catalog (concept "Rule catalog", decision "Rules live in their
artifacts"): one way for each artifact kind to declare or implement a rule id, a test in the tooling's build that
fails on a duplicate id, a checked rule without implementation or a message without its link, the first rules of
scope listing and site, and a rule page on the docs site read from the artifacts.

## Key decisions
- A rule is declared once, by a rule block (a fenced block with info string `rule`: id, scope, severity,
  enforcement) right under the heading of the section that explains it: skills/**/*.md for guided and checked
  rules, review/**/*.md for reviewed rules. A checked rule is still explained in a skill, which is what the
  assistant reads.
- Implementations carry only the id and the link: lint/rules/<id>.ts (file name = id, meta.docs.url), check/rules/*.ts
  (default export { id, url, ... }). The link must be https://lernapps.net/tooling/rules/#<id>, the rule's entry on
  the rule page. Ids are unique per kind, so a lint rule and a check may implement the same rule.
- scripts/rules.ts reads the artifacts (`test`: the id test; `page`: the rule page); nothing is generated into the
  artifacts. test/rules.test.ts runs it, so it is part of `lernapps check`; scripts/build.sh writes _site/rules/.
- Scope may be a list: no-request-before-click and no-tracking are both listing criteria and rules of every page on
  lernapps.net; ch. 8 says "one or more of".
- The first rules are placeholders in their future artifacts: skills/lernapps-app/SKILL.md (no-request-before-click,
  no-tracking, no-cookies, readable-without-javascript, wcag-aa, usable-at-360px, legal-links) and review/rubric.md
  (runs-in-browser, no-account, free-of-charge, no-ads, learners-act). The skill rules are `guided` until steps 3
  and 4 add their checks and lint rules and switch them to `checked`; the id test then demands the implementation.

## Side effects (if any)
tsconfig.json includes check/ and lint/ for the coming checks and lint rules. The skill folder makes the repo a
source for `npx skills add lernapps/tooling`, with a placeholder skill holding real rules. The docs site has a new
page, /tooling/rules/, linked from the start page.

## Intent
Reconcile the rule convention with the skill lernapps-app from step 5: its 15 rules were HTML comment placeholders
waiting for this convention, and several of its ids name the same requirements as this branch's first rules.

## Key decisions
- Every rule is declared once, by a rule block in the skill section that explains it, whatever its enforcement:

  and review); `free-of-charge`, `no-ads` and `no-account` leave the text of `no-tracking` and become their own
  `reviewed` rules, with `runs-in-browser`.

  listing criteria and rules of every page on lernapps.net.

message:
refactor(rules): unique ids per artifact kind, rule list by id, agent review instead of cross-checks (#30)

* refactor(rules): unique ids per artifact kind, a rule list by id, an agent review instead of cross-checks

## Intent

The same rule may be told preventively in a skill and checked by a lint rule or check under the same id. The id
test forbade that (one enforcement per rule) and cross-checked the artifacts, which needs metadata in every
artifact. Make each artifact kind stand alone and leave agreement between them to an agent's review.

## Key decisions

- Ids are unique within each kind of artifact: skills, checks, lint rules, rubric. No check that an implementation
  is declared in a skill, or that a declared rule is implemented.
- The rule block drops `enforcement`; it keeps `id`, `scope`, `severity`.
- `npm run rules` (`node scripts/rules.ts list`) prints every rule grouped by id as YAML, with what each artifact
  says; the rule page reads the same grouping.
- The skill `rules-review` (`.agents/skills/`) has an agent read that list and report drift, gaps, moves and
  overlaps in YAML; it changes nothing.
- Architecture (concept rule catalog, decision rules in artifacts, glossary, risk, runtime view) and the plan
  (KD-22) say the same.

## Side effects

- The rule page no longer shows an enforcement column; each rule lists the artifacts that carry it.

author: Oliver Jägle
message:
feat(check): lernapps check runs the checks of the built app and reports in YAML (#31)

* feat(check): lernapps check runs the checks of the built app and reports in YAML

## Intent
One check command for hooks, CI and the listing validation (issue #12): the toolchain
steps of a repo plus the checks of the built app, on a bundle or a URL without the repo,
with a catalog entry checked against the app, and one report shape that people and
assistants can act on.

## Key decisions
- The CLI runs whatever exists and decides nothing from rule metadata: every module in
  check/rules/ runs and returns undefined when its input (built app, repo, entry, --site)
  is missing; its rule is then left out of `rules` in the report. The heavy part builds
  with `vp build` when the repo has index.html (an app), else `vp pack` (a package),
  checks dist/ when it has index.html, and runs `playwright test` when
  playwright.config.* exists.
- Each page reachable from the start page is visited once in Chromium without a click;
  requests to other hosts are recorded and blocked, so no check depends on another
  server and the same input gives the same report. The browser is installed once on
  the first launch (Playwright caches it); when none can run, the finding says how to
  install it.
- New checks, each with its own rule id and url: no-request-before-click, no-tracking,
  readable-without-javascript, usable-at-360px, accessible (axe-core, WCAG 2.1 A/AA),
  links-resolve, dependency-licence (repo only, allowlist of SPDX ids), site-check
  (calls lernapps-check of @lernapps/site with --site), entry-links-resolve and
  entry-fitness-matches (--entry). Toolchain step failures are findings of the skill
  rule checks-pass. Skill sections for the new ids where an assistant can prevent the
  problem.
- A passing run prints one line; otherwise the YAML report on stdout; --report always
  writes it. Its JSON Schema is exported by the package and published on the docs site.
- A failed run with --pre-push increments prePushFailures in .vibe/plan.md; CI (no flag)
  does not count.
- Step output is shown only when the step fails.
- Tests run the real CLI on fixture apps (one passing, one per broken rule), on a URL,
  with --entry and --site, and in temporary app repos; the installed package runs the
  checks from dist/.

## Side effects
- yaml and @lernapps/site move to dependencies; playwright and axe-core are new
  dependencies.
- `npm run rules` shows the severity of checks.
- The pre-push part of this repo also runs the dependency licence check.

author: Oliver Jägle
message:
feat(preset): the shared preset, its lint plugin and the git hooks every app extends (#34)

* feat(preset): the shared preset, its lint plugin and the git hooks every app extends

## Intent

Step 4 of the tooling for agentic app creation (#13): what every app imports and never edits. An app that only
extends the preset (one-line vite.config.ts, tsconfig.json and the prepare script) gets every lint rule and both git
hooks without configuration of its own, so a rule or hook changed in the package reaches every app with the next
version.

## Key decisions

- The shared base lives in archetypes/shared/: `lernapps(config?)` (@lernapps/tooling/preset) is the vite-plus
  configuration (lint with the plugin and each rule's severity, no `any`, type-aware with type check; format; unit
  tests; staged files; `base: "./"`), merged with the app's own settings. Strict tsconfig base, Playwright
  configuration (desktop and 360 px), and runtime helpers: storage on the device under the app's prefix with
  try/catch, a translator for the message files, announce/moveFocus for assistive technology.
- The helpers are typed by their TypeScript sources (`types` condition) and run from dist/, built by `vp pack`
  next to the CLI; vite-plus is a peer dependency at the version the preset is written for.
- The hooks are scripts in the package (archetypes/shared/hooks/), installed by vite-plus's own dispatcher:
  the app's prepare script runs `vp config --hooks-dir node_modules/@lernapps/tooling/archetypes/shared/hooks`.
  Pre-commit: `vp staged`, then `lernapps check --pre-commit`; pre-push: `lernapps check --pre-push`, which
  already counts a failure in prePushFailures.
- The lint plugin (lint/plugin.ts, @lernapps/tooling/lint) is an Oxlint JS plugin on the ESLint-compatible API;
  each rule is lint/rules/<id>.ts and every message ends with the link to its rule. Rules: no-request-before-click
  (URLs of other hosts in code; reuses the id of the check and the skill), storage-through-wrapper,
  learner-text-german (texts written into the page from strings; reuses the skill's id), suppression-reason
  (disable comments need rules and `-- reason`; no @ts-ignore/@ts-nocheck; @ts-expect-error with a reason).
  `any` stays with Oxlint's own typescript/no-explicit-any, set in the preset.
- Skill lernapps-app: new sections suppression-reason (moved from fix-from-message), keep-the-preset,
  strict-typescript, storage-through-wrapper; no-request-before-click and learner-text-german say how the lint
  rules are met.
- Tested end to end: a fixture app installed from git that only extends the preset; commit stopped by a lint
  violation with the rule's message, push stopped by a request to another host with prePushFailures + 1, a clean
  commit and push (unit and Playwright tests included), and each lint rule's verdict on source snippets.

## Side effects

- package.json: new exports (preset, tsconfig.json, playwright, storage, i18n, a11y, lint), `archetypes` in
  files, vite-plus as peer dependency; the package build bundles the new entries.
- Architecture, chapter 5: archetype presets, git hooks and lint rules describe how they are built.

author: Claude
message:
feat(quiz): lernapps create and the quiz archetype

## Intent
The first archetype, as a deep scaffold: `lernapps create --archetype quiz` plus a question bank gives an app that
passes `lernapps check` without further code. The creator's assistant writes only the questions and their options.

## Key decisions
- Generator (`generator/create.ts`, `lernapps create`): copies the archetype's folder of lernapps/app-templates at
  the commit pinned in package.json (`appTemplates`), fetched with git; `--templates <repo>` or
  `LERNAPPS_TEMPLATES` names a local clone instead, so the tests never fetch from GitHub. It writes AGENTS.md, the
  plan (kept when already there, else the template starting in Code), `pages.yml` (site-check and site-deploy, which
  run `lernapps check` through the app's `check` script), the content-error issue form, LICENSE and renovate.json
  (`generator/app/`). It fails on an unknown archetype (exit 2) and on a folder that holds anything but `.git` and
  the plan (exit 1). `--tooling <spec>` sets the package the app depends on, for the tests.
- Quiz engine in the package (`archetypes/quiz/`), the template stays thin: the preset `quiz()` adds a build step
  that validates `src/quiz.json` and renders every question into index.html, so the page is a worksheet with its
  answer key without JavaScript; the engine shows one question at a time in the order of `?seed=<n>`, opens
  `#frage-<id>`, gives feedback per option, the score and the solutions at the end. Nothing is stored unless the
  bank sets `rememberLastResult` (then through the preset's storage).
- Question bank: JSON with a JSON Schema (`quiz.v1.schema.json`, published under /tooling/schemas/), validated with
  ajv plus checks the schema cannot express (one correct option in a single choice, unique ids and options);
  each problem names the question by position and id. ajv moves to dependencies, the build step needs it.
- `@lernapps/tooling/quiz/e2e`: generic Playwright tests for any bank (deep link, right and wrong answer per
  question, full score, no JavaScript), so every quiz app has end-to-end tests of its own content.
- Skill `lernapps-quiz` with eight rules of scope `archetype:quiz`; `quiz-bank-valid` is decided by the build.
- Tests: end to end through the real CLI on a temporary app installed from git (test/create.e2e.test.ts), unit
  tests only for the scoring. CI checks out app-templates at the pinned commit for them.

## Side effects
- The pin points at app-templates' main until the template is pushed; the next commit moves it.
- The architecture names the generator's options and the question bank as an interface of the archetype presets.

author: Oliver Jägle
message:
feat(review): review procedure with prompt, rubric per archetype and verdict schema (#33)

* feat(review): review procedure with prompt, rubric per archetype and verdict schema

## Intent
The formal validation's judgment part: an agent in a fresh context reviews an app that asks to be
listed, starting from the validation report, and writes a verdict bound to the reviewed commit, in
which every finding names a rule id or proposes a new rule and where it would act. The owner runs it
in the environment for lernapps agents and decides on the listing.

## Key decisions
- review/prompt.md is the prompt the owner gives a fresh agent in a checkout of this repo: prepare
  a work directory in .reviews/ (ignored), clone the app at the commit, build the bundle, run
  lernapps check for the report, then read the report, the rule catalog, the plan and its
  retrospective, the rubric, the bundle, the dependencies and the history; judge; write
  verdict.yaml; check it; hand it to the owner, who posts it on the listing pull request.
- The rubric is review/rubric.md for every app plus review/archetypes/<name>.md per archetype.
  Every level-2 heading of a rubric file is an item and needs its rubric block: the id test reports
  an item without one.
- New rules, each with a rubric item and a skill section: no-learner-data-in-texts (listing,
  error), correct-content-support (listing, hint), topic-has-exercises (archetype:explainer),
  start-page-explains (archetype:interactive), quiz-feedback-explains (archetype:quiz). Reused as
  rubric items: learner-text-german (plain language), no-tracking (after a click), third-party-licence
  and retrospective-filled.
- The verdict is YAML with a JSON Schema (review/verdict.v1.schema.json), exported by the package
  and published on the docs site. outcome is fail exactly when a finding has severity error. A
  verdict check (npm run verdict -- <file>) validates the schema and the catalog: every rule id
  exists, every proposal is new.
- CI calls no model: a verdict recorded for a fixture app with a planted ad is tested. The fixture
  repo is committed with a fixed author and date, so its commit is the same everywhere, and a
  change to the fixture fails the test until the verdict is recorded again.

## Side effects
- package.json: export and file review/verdict.v1.schema.json, script verdict.
- .gitignore keeps the built bundle of review fixtures and ignores .reviews/.
- Architecture: the review procedure block, a new interface for the verdict, the listing scenario,
  the environment for lernapps agents, the rule catalog and stable contracts, a new decision and a
  glossary term.

refactor(quiz): the quiz runtime moves to @lernapps/app-templates, a knowledge quiz

## Intent
The owner's decision: an archetype's runtime is a package the app depends on, in lernapps/app-templates, so a new
feature reaches an app with a dependency bump; the tooling stays a development dependency. And the quiz becomes a
quiz about things to know: background knowledge on every option, further reading on every question.

## Key decisions
- The engine, the build step, the stylesheet, the generic end-to-end tests, the schema and the scoring's unit tests
  leave `archetypes/quiz/` for the root package of app-templates (`@lernapps/app-templates/quiz`, `/quiz/plugin`,
  `/quiz/style.css`, `/quiz/e2e`). The tooling never depends on it; ajv is a development dependency again.
- The shared preset is unchanged: the app's vite.config.ts is `lernapps({ plugins: [quiz()] })`. The rule
  keep-the-preset names that form.
- The generator sets the app's `@lernapps/app-templates` to the commit it copied the template from (`github:` for
  GitHub, `git+file://` for a local clone, so the tests stay offline) and removes the template's `.npmrc`. The
  archetypes it knows are listed with the pin (`appTemplates.archetypes`).
- The schema keeps its URL under /tooling/schemas/: the docs build takes it from app-templates at the pinned commit
  (the clone in LERNAPPS_TEMPLATES, or git).
- Skill lernapps-quiz: the new bank (`info`, `link`, `links`, `sources`), the example from "Naturwunder der Welt";
  `quiz-feedback-explains` is about `info` and `explanation`; new rules `quiz-further-reading` (warning) and
  `quiz-own-words` (warning: copied Wikipedia text breaks its licence, but whether a sentence is one's own is judged,
  not checked).
- Architecture: the decision `dec-runtime-package`; `dec-templates-repo` and `dec-archetypes` name the runtime;
  the block of the templates holds the runtimes and provides the runtime and the question bank.
- The fixture bank is the template's "Naturwunder der Welt", with `rememberLastResult`; the generator test checks
  the background, the marks, the explanation and the links after each answer and in the answer key.
- CI checks out app-templates with its history, so npm can install the runtime from the clone.

## Side effects
- The pin moves to the head of app-templates' branch feat/15-quiz-runtime.

author: Claude
message:
fix(hooks): install an app's hooks only where the app is the root of its repository

The quiz template's prepare script ran vp config, which installs the hook
dispatcher into the enclosing git repository: npm install in app-templates'
quiz/ pointed the whole app-templates repo at the template's hooks, and commits
at its root failed. `lernapps hooks` installs the hooks only where the current
folder is the root of its git work tree and otherwise says why it changed
nothing. The generator writes it as every app's prepare script, so a template
needs none of its own.

The create e2e test covers both: the generated app at the root of its repo gets
the hooks; the same app in a folder of another repo leaves that repo's
core.hooksPath unset after npm install.

## Intent

## Key decisions

+- [ ] 11 · The explainer archetype ([#19](https://github.com/lernapps/tooling/issues/19)): first an MVP based on the
+  Mathe-Karte, sketched below for the owner's review before anything is built. The issue's "prototype first" (Eleventy

 - [ ] 10 · Evals for the quiz archetype ([#18](https://github.com/lernapps/tooling/issues/18))
-- [ ] 11 · The explainer archetype, after the rendering prototype ([#19](https://github.com/lernapps/tooling/issues/19))
 - [ ] 12 · The interactive archetype ([#20](https://github.com/lernapps/tooling/issues/20))
 - [ ] Open points of the documentation site ([#6](https://github.com/lernapps/tooling/issues/6))
 
+### Sketch: the explainer MVP (step 11, for the owner's review)
+
+*Proposal of 2026-10-13. Sources: KD-02, KD-06, KD-09, KD-11, KD-21; issue #19; the Mathe-Karte (lernapps/mathe-karte:
+`src/prozent/`, `src/kern/`, `src/_includes/kompetenz.njk`, `lib/bild.js`, `lib/pruefungen.js`, `e2e/`,
+`test/apps/vertrag.test.js`, `werkzeuge/skill/lern-app/`, `werkzeuge/review/ki-review.md`); the quiz archetype
+(app-templates `quiz/`, `runtime/quiz/`; tooling `generator/`, `archetypes/shared/`, skills, `review/`).*
+
+**What the Mathe-Karte is.** Eleventy 3 over plain JavaScript, one shared kern, ~20 apps. Per app a config (`APP`,
+`KOMPETENZEN`), per topic ("Kompetenz") a Markdown file with front matter only: `warum`, `regel`, `beispiel` as
+free HTML, `bild`, `video`, `serlo`. One layout renders Warum, Regel, Beispiel, Bild, Video, Übung. Per topic a
+generator and checker in free JS (`erzeugeAufgabe(zufall, vorgaben)`, `pruefeAntwort`): seeded "nice" numbers,
+several contexts with text templates, typical mistakes diagnosed with their own message, a Rechenweg. Pictures: one
+drawing function per topic renders static SVG at build (a mini DOM) and redraws it in the browser. Formulas: plain
+text in `<code>` (`W = G · p / 100`), no renderer. Per app also a start page with self-assessment, a test page,
+`llms.txt` and a tutor prompt. Its rules come from tests and build checks: generator contract for every topic
+(deterministic per seed, the solution passes, nonsense fails), the picture does not give the answer away, plausible
+numbers, files under 500 lines, no external resources, dead links, the tutor link allowlist; Playwright for no-JS,
+360 px, axe, external requests.
+- **Explainer** (static): Warum, Regel, Beispiel, the formulas, the picture of the example, sources.
+- **Interactive**: the exercise (generator, input, checker, feedback, Rechenweg, picture of the task), self-assessment,
+  test page, video embed after a click.
+- Without JavaScript its exercises show only "Für die Übungsaufgaben brauchst du JavaScript". The MVP does better.
+
+#### 1. Scope of the MVP
+- One topic family: **Prozent** (Klasse 7/8), three topics: Prozentwert, Prozentsatz, Grundwert. Each page: Warum,
+  Regel (with formulas), Beispiel, a figure, an exercise; a start page lists the topics in order.
+- One interactive exercise type, `calculation`: generated numbers, one numeric answer, feedback with diagnosed
+  mistakes, hint, Rechenweg, a figure of the task.
+- Two figure kinds drawn from data: `hundred-grid` (Hunderterfeld) and `bar` (Prozentstreifen); plus `image`, a
+  bundled SVG or PNG with alt text, source and licence.
+- `llms.txt` generated from the content (pages, deep links), because it is derived data and costs little.
+- Left out: test page, self-assessment, videos and other embeds after a click, the tutor prompt and its allowlist,
+  further exercise types (terms, fractions, choice, clickable figures), variables as URL parameters (only `seed`),
+  the curriculum map across apps, several apps in one repo.
+
+#### 2. The authoring model
+The creator's assistant writes content as data and no code, as in the quiz. Options:
+
+| | A: YAML per topic, schema at build | B: Markdown with front matter | C: Eleventy templates in TypeScript (`.11ty.ts`, KD-02) |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Prose | restricted Markdown in fields | Markdown body | free templates |
+| What a schema covers | everything | front matter only; the body needs a parser with rules | types only |
+| Free HTML or code | none | needs HTML off and directives for figures and exercises | anything |
+| Deterministic validation | high | medium | low |
+
+**Recommended: A.** `src/app.yaml` (title, intro, order of topics, sources) and `src/topics/<id>.yaml`, both
+validated against `explainer.v1.schema.json` at build (published at lernapps.net/tooling/schemas/, as the quiz's).
+YAML rather than JSON, because the content is long German prose (block scalars, no escaping); the schema is the same
+kind as the quiz's and the editor finds it by a `yaml-language-server` comment. The fields are fixed: `id`, `title`,
+`summary`, `why`, `rule`, `example`, `figure`, `exercise`, `links`. Prose fields are restricted Markdown: paragraphs,
+bold, lists, tables, links, `$…$` for formulas; raw HTML is a build error.
+- **Formulas:** one notation, a LaTeX subset in `$…$` (`\frac`, `\cdot`, `\%`, `\text`, `^`, `_`, `\sqrt`,
+  `\approx`, `\pm`, parentheses), rendered at build to MathML (Temml, MIT, MathML only, no fonts, no script). A
+  command outside the list or a parse error fails the build with file, field and formula. MathML Core shows in
+  current Chromium, Firefox and Safari, and screen readers read it.
+- **Figures:** declared kinds with parameters, rendered at build to inline SVG with `role="img"` and an accessible
+  name from the required `caption`. The same pure function (SVG as a string, no DOM) draws the task's figure in the
+  browser. `image` requires `alt`, `source` and `licence`.
+- **Exercises:** declared widget types configured as data. A `calculation` has `variants` (text template, unit,
+  value ranges or lists per variable), `require` (conditions for "nice" numbers), `answer` (an expression and the
+  number format: `number` or `money`, decimals), `mistakes` (expression and message each), `hint`, `steps`
+  (formulas with placeholders) and `figure`. Expressions are a small arithmetic language on exact fractions
+  (`+ - * /`, parentheses, numbers, declared variables, `round(x, n)`), parsed by the runtime; there is no eval and no
+  app code. A Mathe-Karte generator like `prozentwert.js` becomes about 25 lines of YAML.
+
+Why: a schema and a parser decide everything the creator writes, and the runtime renders it, so readable without
+JavaScript, accessible markup and working deep links hold by construction and are tested once in the runtime. What
+the Mathe-Karte proves with per-topic tests (deterministic, the solution passes, nonsense fails, the figure does not
+give the answer away) becomes generic checks on the data. The cost: what the data model cannot say needs a new widget
+type in the runtime, not code in the app (Q3).
+
+#### 3. What the runtime provides
+In `@lernapps/app-templates`, next to the quiz, under `runtime/explainer/`, with the same exports:
+- `explainer/plugin`: the Vite plugin `explainer()`. It reads and validates the content, renders the start page and
+  one page per topic (`<id>/index.html`) into the shell `index.html` (marker `<!-- explainer -->`), plus `llms.txt`;
+  it renders formulas, figures and the no-JS form of each exercise; it injects the one client module and stylesheet
+  into every page. It fails the build on any file in `src/` outside the content and `main.ts`.
+- `explainer`: `startExplainer()`, which enhances each exercise in place. It uses the same pure modules as the build
+  for generator, checker, number format and figures, moves the focus to the feedback (lesson of app-templates#10), and
+  stores nothing.
+- `explainer/style.css` and `messages/de.json`: the layout. Header with the app's title, back to the start page,
+  previous and next topic, footer with sources and licences; mobile-first, 360 px.
+- `explainer/e2e`: `explainerTests()`, the generic end-to-end tests, read from the app's content (7.).
+- `explainer/explainer.v1.schema.json`.
+
+The template `explainer/` holds only thin files and example content, as `quiz/` does: `vite.config.ts` is
+`lernapps({ plugins: [explainer()] })`, `src/main.ts` two lines, `e2e/explainer.e2e.ts` two lines, the shared
+`playwright.config.ts`, and the three Prozent topics as the example.
+
+#### 4. The no-JS contract
+- Every page is complete static HTML: all text, every formula as MathML, every figure as inline SVG, links, sources.
+  The script only adds; it hides and replaces nothing that is there without it.
+- Each exercise renders, without JS, three worked tasks from fixed seeds: task text, figure, and a `<details>`
+  "Lösung" with the Rechenweg and the answer. Native `<details>` needs no script. With JS, the live exercise appears
+  above them: input, "Prüfen", feedback, "Neue Aufgabe", deep link `<id>/?seed=<n>#uebung`. No `<noscript>` saying
+  that JavaScript is needed.
+- Checked deterministically:
+  - by construction: the runtime renders everything the content says;
+  - by `explainerTests()` with JavaScript off, for every page of the content: the heading and every section are
+    visible, the number of `<math>` elements equals the formulas in the data, every figure is visible with its name,
+    and every worked task's solution opens and shows the answer that the checker accepts. This runs in
+    `lernapps check --pre-push`, in the hooks and in CI;
+  - at the gate (Q4): a check of `lernapps check`, scoped to pages the runtime marks as explainer pages
+    (`<meta name="lernapps-archetype" content="explainer">`). It visits them without JavaScript and finds
+    sections, formulas and figures. It works on a deployed URL, so the listing validation and `/review` run it too.
+
+#### 5. Rules
+The owner removed the site rules and readable-without-JavaScript for apps in general (#47, #49). For the explainer it
+comes back as an **archetype rule** (`archetype:explainer`), because it is what the archetype promises (KD-02). Apps
+of other archetypes stay unbound.
+
+| Id | Severity | Enforced by |
+|---|---|---|
+| `explainer-only-data`: write only `src/app.yaml`, `src/topics/*.yaml` and bundled figure files | error | build (no other files in `src/`), skill, rubric; with `keep-the-preset` |
+| `explainer-content-valid`: the content validates (schema, unique ids, every reference and placeholder declared) | error | build, one line per problem with file and path |
+| `explainer-formulas-static`: formulas only in `$…$`, in the one notation, rendered at build | error | build (parse, command list); rubric for formulas left as plain text |
+| `explainer-readable-without-js`: every page, formula, figure and worked task reads without JavaScript | error | `explainerTests()`; `lernapps check` (Q4); rubric |
+| `explainer-exercises-sound`: for 200 seeds per exercise the conditions hold, the answer is finite with the declared decimals, no mistake gives the right answer, the task's figure does not show the answer | error | build (sampling with fixed seeds); `explainerTests()` checks right, wrong and each mistake in the browser |

docs(plan): explainer sketch revised after the owner's review

## Intent

The owner reviewed the explainer sketch and asked for a model that carries
other subjects than maths, reuses more of the quiz, and has a fixed
structure, before anything is built.

## Key decisions

- A page is an ordered list of blocks from a closed set (text, formula,
  figure, labelled-figure, table, timeline, definition, quote, code, example,
  note, section), each rendered at build. Warum, Regel, Beispiel becomes a
  recommended page structure in the skill.
- Formulas in one LaTeX subset with Temml; its mhchem extension renders
  \ce and \pu to MathML (tried in Node with Temml 0.14.0).
- Exercises are the quiz's six question types as blocks, with the quiz
  runtime's validation, checker and solution rendering, plus calculation for
  maths and the sciences.
- Four levels (app, chapter, page, two section levels), explicit and complete
  order lists, ids as paths, a shape without chapters for small apps,
  generated navigation without JS; structure rules with ids.
- A second fixture that is not maths (history, without chapters).
- Two new open questions (depth, the shape without chapters).
- The plan's note on org rules no longer says readable without JavaScript
  for every app.

## Side effects (if any)

None. Only the plan file changes.

docs(plan): explainer sketch with generated exercises, Vue components, languages

## Intent

The owner reviewed the revised explainer sketch and decided more before
anything is built: a property-based exercise notation, Vue components,
several languages and mandatory chapters.

## Key decisions

- `generated` replaces `calculation`: arbitraries (`given`), preconditions
  (`where`), task, answer with a comparator from the quiz's answer kinds,
  mistakes, hint and steps; the build runs it as a property test over fixed
  seeds. Examples for maths, history and chemistry.
- `vue-component` blocks: single-file components with typed props, rendered
  at build and hydrated as islands; props validated against their types; an
  exercise contract whose logic module is property-tested at build; build and
  lint checks for network, HTML injection, imports, browser globals, size;
  a test file per component. Rules with ids, shared later with step 12.
- Languages: every text a string or a language map, German first and
  required, one page tree per language.
- Chapters mandatory; a single chapter is hidden in the navigation but kept
  in the URL.
- The owner's decisions recorded in KD-02 and the sketch; language maps and
  the chapter in the URL listed as confirmations (Q7, Q8); Q3 rewritten.

## Side effects (if any)

None. Only the plan file changes.

docs(plan): explainer sketch decided; nojs for components, sections not headings

## Intent

The owner agreed to every remaining proposal of the explainer sketch and
added two points, so the sketch is the decided basis for implementation.

## Key decisions

- Every learner-facing text field takes restricted Markdown; a heading in a
  text field is a build error that says to use a section block
  (`explainer-structure-by-sections`). Rejected: silent conversion.
- Every `vue-component` block requires a localisable `nojs` text, rendered
  in place; the server-side render stays hidden until hydration and is not
  relied on for the no-JS contract (`vue-component-nojs`).
- The open questions became a list of owner decisions of 2026-10-13; KD-02
  and KD-06 now say the explainer renders with a Vite plugin, Eleventy as the
  fallback.

## Side effects (if any)

None. Only the plan file changes.

author: Claude
message:
feat(check): visit every page of a bundle; on a URL, say when the limit stops the visit

A bundle has a finite list of pages, so its check visits all of them: first the
pages reachable by links from the start page, then every other .html file. A page
no link from the start page reaches is an error of the new rule pages-reachable.
The 404 page at the root and files without <!doctype html> are no pages; a page
marked noindex is checked but need not be reached. On a URL the check keeps its
limit of 100 pages and, when it stops there, says so in a hint of the same rule
instead of stopping silently. Pages are visited four at a time, in the order one
at a time would visit them.

message:
test(check): prove the visit's limits on a tiny app, in the fast set

The limit of a check of an app on a URL can be lowered for the tooling's own tests
(LERNAPPS_TEST_URL_PAGE_LIMIT, not a flag and not in the help). With a limit of 3, a
five-page app shows the same as the 120-page app did: the bundle is visited beyond
the limit, the orphan is an error of pages-reachable, a noindex page is checked but
need not be reached, 404.html is not visited, and the URL run reports the hint. It
takes about 5 s instead of 35 s, so it moves from the heavy set to the fast set.

author: Claude
message:
feat: the change scope decides what hooks and CI run

A central classifier, `lernapps changes` (changes/changes.ts): a change of only the
plan (.vibe/**) is none, only docs (docs/**/*.md) and the plan is docs, anything
else, or changed files that cannot be known, is all. The lists are allowlists, with
a default map per kind of repo (app, tooling, site) and validated exceptions in
package.json (lernapps.changes: kind, none, docs, all).

- lernapps check --pre-commit/--pre-push ask it first: none, and docs in an app,
  print one line and check nothing; docs in a repo with a site check the site.
- The tooling's pre-push hook folds its heavy-path gating into the same patterns
  and sources; docs build and check the docs site only.
- app-check and app-publish classify the event themselves: none and docs skip.
- A reusable workflow changes.yml outputs the scope; the tooling's workflows gate
  their jobs on it, with one always-running final job as the required check.
- The generated pages.yml drops its paths-ignore.

author: Claude
message:
feat: the archetype explainer: pin, vue-tsc in the type step, component lint rules

## Intent
Step 6 of the explainer MVP: `lernapps create --archetype explainer` gives an app that passes `lernapps check`,
with the checks of its Vue components in the editor and the commit's part of the check, as the build of
app-templates checks them.

## Key decisions
- The pin moves to app-templates 1af96d3 (every runtime step of the explainer merged), and `explainer` joins
  `appTemplates.archetypes`.
- `lernapps check` runs `vue-tsc --noEmit` after `vp check` only where the project has a `.vue` file, so apps
  without components pay nothing. The generator gives an explainer app `vue-tsc` and `typescript` as dev
  dependencies, at the versions of app-templates; a missing vue-tsc is a finding that says how to add it.
- Four lint rules with the ids and wording of the build checks: `vue-component-no-network`,
  `-no-html-injection`, `-imports`, `-browser-globals`. They act on a component's code: a `.vue` file's
  `<script setup>` (Oxlint does not reach the template, so `v-html` stays the build's) and the modules of
  `src/components/` except their tests. A global is a name no scope of the file declares, since Oxlint's
  isGlobalReference knows only configured globals.
- `learner-text-german` leaves component code alone: a component gets its texts through its props from the
  content, where the build checks every language. `storage-through-wrapper` already reaches `.vue` files; a
  snippet proves it.
- create.e2e gets a minimal explainer part in the heavy set: create, install, check, update, and a component
  with a type error failing in vue-tsc (about 35 s plus the install).

## Side effects (if any)
The generator writes devDependencies sorted by name, as the formatter keeps them.

author: Claude
message:
fix(renovate): the building blocks wait for a three-hour window, not minutes

The group "lernapps building blocks" bumped every repo within minutes of each
tooling merge, so open workflow pull requests conflicted again and again. It
now opens its pull request only in the hours 0, 3, ... 21: tooling commits
merged in between arrive together, on average about an hour later.

Not minimumReleaseAge: only the actions (github-digest) have a release
timestamp. The npm git pin (github-tags, no currentValue) and the git-refs
managers have none, and with the default timestamp-required and the
internalChecksFilter strict of the extended preset Renovate holds them back
for good, while the timestamped actions would move alone: a partial bump.
minimumReleaseAge stays 0 so that every pin moves. Automerge stays on.

## Intent
Step 7 of the explainer MVP (Q4): the gate checks what the explainer promises without JavaScript, on a bundle and on
a deployed app, so the listing validation and /review check it too; an entry's topic that links a section must
find it.

## Key decisions
- Only pages with `<meta name="lernapps-archetype" content="explainer">` get the second visit #47 removed: one more
  browser context with JavaScript off, made at the first marked page and shared by all of them, opened while the
  rest of the page's visit runs. Other apps get no context and no visit, and the rule is left out of their report.
- Without JavaScript, every `<details>` opened: an h1; each heading, `<math>` and figure visible, a figure with its
  accessible name; each `.explainer-exercise` with a "Lösung" that is not empty; each component's `nojs` text
  visible and not empty. The parts the runtime fills only with JavaScript (island, live task, a question's controls
  and reveal) are not read. No formula count against the content: a URL has no content; `explainerTests()` keeps it.

  content where the creator can act (alt text, `nojs`), else the runtime's issue tracker.
- A topic's `#<section>` (also `#<section>/<sub>`) must be the id of an element of its page, read from the HTML as
  the server sends it, in the same fetch that checks the page: no browser.
- pages-reachable needed no change: the template and both app-templates fixtures give no finding.

message:
feat(generator): every app gets its content guide, checked by app-content-guide

## Intent
The content decisions of a first run (curriculum, competencies, exercise patterns, figures, sources) live only in
the plan and the conversation; an agent that extends the app later sees neither. Every app now keeps them in an
app-local skill, `.agents/skills/app-content/SKILL.md`, which the generator writes as a skeleton.

## Key decisions
- The skeleton has nine fixed headings and a marked placeholder (`<!-- FILL IN: … -->`) under each; its
  frontmatter description makes a harness load it for any content work in the app.
- `.claude/skills/app-content` is a relative symbolic link to the guide's folder, for Claude Code. Git keeps it as a
  link (mode 120000), so it survives the commit and a clone. Where the system allows no symbolic link (Windows
  without Developer Mode) the generator leaves it out and says so; a Windows checkout without core.symlinks gets a
  small text file in its place, which no harness takes for a skill. AGENTS.md names the guide's own path, so every
  harness still finds it.
- The check `app-content-guide` (error) runs on an app built with the tooling: one with a plan file that depends on
  the runtime @lernapps/app-templates. The guide must exist with its headings; placeholders fail once the app has
  content, i.e. once the plan is in Commit, for both archetypes: by then the creator's questions (quiz) or chapters
  (explainer) are built in place of the generated example, which a check cannot tell from the creator's content
  without the template.
- `lernapps update` adds the skeleton and the link to an app made before, so the new error has a one-command fix.

## Side effects (if any)
Listed apps in Commit fail `lernapps check` until their guide is added and filled in.

## Intent
Before the next full creator run (an electricity explainer), the assistant needs guidance for what an app teaches:
the curriculum, its competencies and sources, the exercises, and how the app grows later. The archetype skills keep
their mechanics and say how each of these is expressed there.

## Key decisions
- `lernapps-content-research`: Land, Schulform, Jahrgang and the creator's material; the official Lehrplan of the
  Land, cited with document, page and unit; competencies as "Ich kann …", one observable skill each, grouped into
  chapters (no split rule); second sources opened and checked (exists, the actual article, exactly this
  competency), no weak matches; the creator's material stays local; never guess units, wording or ids; on rate

planDiff:
diff --git a/.vibe/development-plan-agentic-app-creation.md b/.vibe/development-plan-agentic-app-creation.md
index 7633f15..0e76bba 100644
--- a/.vibe/development-plan-agentic-app-creation.md
+++ b/.vibe/development-plan-agentic-app-creation.md
@@ -342,6 +342,97 @@ evals cover all three archetypes.*

 - [ ] Open points of the documentation site ([#6](https://github.com/lernapps/tooling/issues/6))
 
+### Sketch: the interactive archetype (step 12, for the owner's decision)
+*From the owner's examples and answers (2026-10-16). Open for the owner's decision; the explainer's sketch below is the
+model.*
+
+#### 1. Scope
+Apps whose doing is the content, with no explanation pages:
+- a ten-finger typing trainer like a shooting game: letter groups fly across the screen and burst when typed in time;
+- a Kniffel trainer that plays Kniffel and teaches probability on the way;
+- a careful-reading app: a text in a correct and a faulty version, and the learner marks the mistakes.
+
+They differ in how they render and run (a game loop per frame, turn by turn, task by task) and share the frame and the
+rules. **One archetype**, not one per kind: the kinds become recipes in its skill, as the exercise patterns are for
+content. Boundary to the explainer: an app that needs explanation pages is an explainer with a component; a few
+background sections on the start page or an info view stay interactive.
+
+#### 2. Opinionated where it makes the rules checkable, free where the learning happens
+- **Fixed:** Vue with TypeScript on vite-plus. The component rules the explainer already has (no network, storage only
+  through the wrapper, no `eval`, `innerHTML` or `v-html`, browser globals only once mounted), their build checks on
+  the SFC compiler's output, the lint rules and `vue-tsc` then hold for every interactive app, with no rules per
+  framework.
+- **Free:** the decomposition, the data format, the game logic and the rendering (DOM, SVG or canvas inside a
+  component, a frame loop with `requestAnimationFrame`).
+- **Libraries** (e.g. a canvas library for the game): bundled, never from a CDN; a licence the licence check accepts;
+  inside a size budget for the whole app, not per component.
+
+#### 3. The shell and the app
+The runtime `interactive/` in lernapps/app-templates, which the app does not change:
+- the static start page from `src/app.yaml` (what the app does, how to play, which competencies, optional background
+  sections), readable without JavaScript, with a `<noscript>` note, imprint and privacy notice;
+- the app page, a settings dialog (time limit off, less motion, sound off) and pause with Esc; the settings reach the
+  app's core as `settings`;
+- languages, storage, announcements and focus through the existing helpers (`i18n`, `storage`, `a11y`);
+- hash routes for modes and levels, so that an entry's topics point somewhere and `entry-links-resolve` resolves them.
+
+What the agent writes, in folders named by the template:
+- `src/core/`: the logic, pure TypeScript without DOM, deterministic by a seed: `start(seed, settings)`,
+  `step(state, input)`, optionally `tick(state, dt)`;
+- `src/ui/`: Vue components that show the state and turn input into actions;
+- `src/data/`: content as data (lessons, texts with their faulty versions) with the app's own schema;
+- `src/playthroughs/`: playthroughs as data, a sequence of keys with the state or announcement expected after it.
+
+Optional, for apps with tasks (a lesson, a text, a Kniffel situation): the explainer's exercise contract (`seed`,
+`describe`, `about`, `examples`), which brings task numbers in the address and the tutor.
+
+#### 4. The architecture guides the agent: arc42 in the app
+The other archetypes are frameworks whose notation already constrains the app so much that nobody needs to understand
+its architecture. An interactive app is free code, so its architecture is written early and kept current.
+- `docs/arc42/` in the app, in the arc42 DSL (`@doctc/arc42`). The **frame** comes from the tooling and
+  `lernapps update` replaces it, as it replaces the `lernapps-*` skills: the constraints (Vue, no network, state only
+  on the device, time pressure that can be turned off, no flashes), the shell as an external building block with its
+  interfaces, the concepts every app implements, and the basic blocks core, view and data with their intent.
+- The **app's own part**, written by the agent: its building blocks under the basic ones (`parent`, `path`), which
+  concepts each implements, its decisions (e.g. canvas or DOM), and its declared accessibility with the reasons.
+- **Checked:** what arc42 checks by itself, no more. Before a commit, `arc42 diff --staged --strict` (about 0.2 s):
+  a block changed without its prose, and new code under `src/` that no block claims, fail. In `lernapps check`,
+  `arc42 validate` (references, required fields, paths that exist, concepts no block implements). Whether the code
+  keeps to the responsibilities is not checked for now: how to see that depends on the framework, and arc42 does not
+  do it. Accepting a finding with `ARC42_CONSISTENT` is for the agent only with a reason in the plan, as with any
+  other check.
+- **In the creator's plan:** a checkpoint "architecture" in Plan, next to the content method: the blocks in plain
+  words and the sketches. Each increment keeps the architecture current. The review reads it.
+
+#### 5. Accessibility as a declaration
+Accessibility has limits: a shooting game with a time limit will not work with a screen reader. Instead of a promise
+it cannot keep, the app declares what it offers:
+- the start page is always WCAG 2.1 AA and says what the app offers and what not;
+- the app's entry gets a field such as `accessibility`: `keyboard` (full, partial, none), `screenReader`, `timing`
+  (none, adjustable, required), `motion`, and a reason;
+- the checks follow the declaration: `keyboard: full` requires a playthrough by keyboard alone, played in the browser;
+  what is declared is checked, what is excluded is not required. No flashes, always: that is health, not comfort.
+
+**For the owner:** this changes the organisation's rule (WCAG 2.1 AA for every page, ORGANIZATION.md) for the
+declared part of an interactive app, and the entry schema in lernapps/apps.
+
+#### 6. Tests and validation
+- The build plays every playthrough against the core and runs the core's property tests over fixed seeds; the e2e
+  test plays the same keys in the browser (`interactiveTests()`), together with the start page without JavaScript,
+  axe on start page and app page, and the time limit turned off.
+- `lernapps create --archetype interactive` gives an app that passes `lernapps check`.
+
+#### 7. Steps and pull requests
+1. **app-templates:** the runtime `interactive/` (shell, settings, hash routes, the core contract, playthroughs,
+   `interactiveTests()`) and a small template app, e.g. a letter-typing game with an untimed mode.
+2. **tooling:** the archetype `interactive`: pin, preset, the component rules' scope widened, the arc42 frame and
+   `arc42 diff` in the pre-commit hook, `arc42 validate` in the check, the skill `lernapps-interactive` with the
+   recipes (real-time game, turn-based game, text work), the plan template's architecture checkpoint, the rubric.
+3. **lernapps/apps and the organisation:** the `accessibility` field and the changed rule, after the owner's decision.
+4. **A first full run** with the typing shooting game as the pilot: it puts the most pressure on the frame (real
+   time, time pressure, motion, accessibility). The Kniffel trainer second, for the core's tests and the exercise
+   contract. Then the evals (10) with all three archetypes.
+
 ### Sketch: the explainer MVP (step 11, decided by the owner)

author: Claude
message:
fix(check): validate the architecture of the working tree, untracked files included

## Intent

A freshly created interactive app failed `lernapps check` with E011 for every
implementation path: arc42 resolves paths only from `git ls-files`
(docToolchain/arc42-language#128), and nothing is added to git yet after
`git init` (lernapps/apps PR #42, entry-point e2e). Outside a repository arc42
took docs/arc42 as the root and failed the same way.

## Key decisions

- The full check's `arc42 validate --strict` runs on a temporary copy of the
  index (GIT_INDEX_FILE) with every untracked, not ignored file below the app
  added as intent to add: the repository's own index stays as it is and no
  file content goes into git; it costs a few milliseconds.
- Outside a repository the step passes `--root .`, so arc42 lists the files of
  the app's folder.
- The pre-commit step (`arc42 diff --staged --strict`, or validate before the
  first commit) keeps reading the staged state, which is what is committed.
- arc42 has no filesystem mode inside a repository, so no option of arc42 alone.

## Side effects

- The fix text no longer says "git add new files first" for the full check;
  for the pre-commit step it says to stage the files that belong to the commit.
  Skill lernapps-interactive changed the same way.
- The interactive e2e no longer runs `git add --all` before the check: it

author: Claude
message:
fix(publish): deploy even when Pages is off, fail only after the deploy

## Intent

When Pages was off or misconfigured, the publish action stopped before the deploy. After the creator's click Pages
served the old state, and a rerun was refused to the integration (403), so the agent pushed a dummy change.

## Key decisions

- A setup the token may not fix is a warning before the deploy; the check after the deploy fails until the click is
  made. The message keeps found/tried/fix/why/link and says no new run is needed.
- The default-branch advice uses REST (`gh api -X PATCH repos/<o>/<r> -f default_branch=main`): GraphQL may be
  blocked where the assistant runs.

## Side effects

- `publish.ts before` exits 0 on a wrong Pages setup; its tests now expect the warning and the failure of `after`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01CokaJ6YdJLqEGhHnk4MHJp
subject: fix(publish): deploy even when Pages is off, fail only after the deploy

author: Claude
message:
feat(guidance): make the GitHub side transparent from the start

## Intent

The first creator run showed the GitHub side as the main source of trouble: `work` became the default branch, Pages
was off at the first deploy, GraphQL was blocked, a rename cost access, and an early message was taken as a yes.

## Key decisions

- The plan template tells the creator in Explore where the app lives and offers to explain GitHub; a new docs page
  https://lernapps.net/tooling/github/ explains it for humans.
- Branches `main`, `gh-pages`, `work` and the Pages source are set up at the start of Explore, before anything is
  pushed, not in `lernapps create`: the first push (often the plan, by the environment) sets the default branch, and
  `create` pushes nothing. The Commit phase only verifies, and brings `work` into `main` by fast-forward.
- New compact skill `lernapps-github`: tool order, GraphQL may be blocked, 403 means a click (never a dummy push),
  REST checks, listing PR from a fork. AGENTS.md is at its word limit, so it is not referenced there.
- `stop-at-checkpoints`: a message sent before the checkpoint question is not a yes.
- `lernapps-interactive`: guidance for the frame and a full-screen game (overlay, way out, focus, space).

## Side effects

- New guidance test for the branch setup in Explore and no GraphQL `gh repo` commands in the template.

author: Claude
message:
fix(check): judge the commit's arc42 diff instead of failing on every hint

A fresh interactive app's first commit after an earlier one (the plan) ran
`arc42 diff --staged --strict`, which fails on every hint: arc42 diff does
not read .arc42ignore (src/main.ts, src/env.d.ts "not covered"), and it hints
"review architecture element" at every file under an interface's path. The
agent then accepted with ARC42_CONSISTENT, which is the HEAD commit, and went
on to set it in advance.

lernapps check now runs `arc42 diff --staged --format json` and judges it:
consistency findings and new code no block claims fail, with .arc42ignore
applied as validate applies it (H021); review hints are a warning in the
report. ARC42_CONSISTENT accepts only consistency findings, which stay in the
report as a warning; it never accepts new code. The skills say that setting it
without a finding shown is a bypass like --no-verify.

author: Claude
message:
fix(rules): tooling rules never block a listing

The catalog takes apps built in completely different ways, so only the
listing rules may block a listing. A rule of scope tooling (plan-file,
retrospective-filled, checks-pass, ...) is advice at listing: the rule
list gives `atListing: warning` for each one declared an error, the
review reports its findings as warnings, and the verdict check refuses
a tooling finding of severity error, so the outcome never fails on
tooling findings alone. An unticked plan box is no finding of
retrospective-filled; a really skipped phase stays a finding of
explore-before-code or stop-at-checkpoints, as a warning.

The declared severity holds in the app's repo: skills, hooks and checks
enforce as before. The listing validation (`lernapps check --entry`)
checks the bundle or URL without the repo and runs no tooling check.

Removes the restriction that a listing or tooling rule is never a
warning, from scripts/rules.ts, ch. 8 and the rule page.
