   tutor support for the quiz, later ([#86](https://github.com/lernapps/tooling/issues/86))
 - [ ] Open points of the documentation site ([#6](https://github.com/lernapps/tooling/issues/6))
 
+### Sketch: the evals (step 10, inventory and expectations, 2026-10-17)
+*The text an agent reads on its way from a creator's first prompt to a listed app, and what we expect it to do with
+it. Scenarios, prompts and scoring follow from this list. Lessons from earlier runs: comments on
+[#18](https://github.com/lernapps/tooling/issues/18).*
+
+#### 1. Inventory: what we evaluate
+
+Entry points (what a creator pastes or an agent finds first):
+- E1 the build prompt on lernapps.net/apps/build/ (`apps/src/_data/de.js`, `en.js`: `build.start.prompt`);
+- E2 the listing prompt on /enter/ (`list.agent.prompt`);
+- E3 the panel "Lieber frei bauen?", which hands `skills/lernapps-app/references/platform-rules.md` to Lovable,
+  bolt.new or a hand-built app;
+- E4 the llms.txt files: lernapps.net (`lernapps.github.io/src/llms.txt`), apps (`apps/src/llms.njk`), tooling
+  (`site/llms.txt`), docs (`docs/site/llms.txt`);
+- E5 the docs pages an agent is sent to: tooling (`site/index.html`), GitHub (`site/github/index.html`).
+
+Workflow:
+- W1 `guidance/AGENTS.md`, copied into each app;
+- W2 `guidance/plan-template.md` (first version), W3 `guidance/increment-template.md` (every later change), with the
+  front matter schema `guidance/plan-front-matter.v1.schema.json`.
+
+Skills (`skills/`, installed with `npx skills add lernapps/tooling`):
+- S1 `lernapps-app` with `references/platform-rules.md`, `workflow-rules.md`, `tooling-rules.md`,
+  `archetype-rules.md`;
+- S2 the archetypes: `lernapps-quiz`, `lernapps-explainer`, `lernapps-interactive`;
+- S3 content: `lernapps-content-research`, `lernapps-exercise-patterns` (with `references/patterns.md`),
+  `lernapps-content-growth`;
+- S4 `lernapps-github`; S5 `lernapps-listing`;
+- S6 in each app: `.agents/skills/app-content/SKILL.md` (from `generator/app/`), which the agent fills in itself.
+
+Messages the tooling writes for the agent (instructions too, rule `fix-from-message`):
+- M1 the CLI: `--help` and the output of `create`, `update`, `check`, `publish` (`src/cli.ts`, `src/usage.ts`,
+  `publish/`);
+- M2 the findings of the checks and lint rules (`check/rules/`, `lint/rules/`) and of the git hooks;
+- M3 the architecture in interactive apps: `docs/arc42/` copied from app-templates, and the findings of the arc42 gate;
+- M4 the entry schema with its descriptions (`apps/schemas/entry.v1.schema.json`, KD-04);
+- M5 the results comment on the listing pull request (`apps/scripts/listing-comment.mjs`) and the review comment
+  (`apps/scripts/review-comment.mjs`).
+
+The review agent, an agent of its own:
+- R1 `review/prompt.md`, `review/rubric.md`, `review/archetypes/{quiz,explainer,interactive}.md`.
+
+Not evaluated: the skills for our own repos (`.agents/skills/` in tooling and docs), the docs models (biz42, pdt42),
+the organisation files in lernapps/.github. A creator's agent may read them but is not sent there.
+
+#### 2. What we expect of the creator's agent
+
+Each expectation names where the evidence is: T transcript, P plan file, G git and GitHub, C checks and review.
+
+Finding the way:
+- A1 From E1 alone it finds the skill and the plan template and reads them in full from the downloaded file, not from
+  a summary (T).
+- A2 It loads the archetype skill once the archetype is chosen, the content skills in Explore, `lernapps-github` when
+  a GitHub step fails, `lernapps-listing` at the listing checkpoint; no skill it does not need (T).
+- A3 It installs nothing before the plan is confirmed and creates the app with the command the plan names (T, G).
+
+Process (W1–W3):
+- A4 One plan per piece of work, copied complete and unchanged; the phase in the front matter follows the work; every
+  task ticked when done, no box left open at the end (P).
+- A5 Explore before code: no app code before the plan is confirmed (G: first commit with code after the confirmation
+  in T).
+- A6 It stops at every checkpoint and waits; a message sent before the checkpoint question is not the answer (T).
+- A7 The retrospective is filled in, and its numbers match the transcript and the hooks (P against T, G).
+- A8 An increment gets its own plan from the increment template (P).
+
+With the creator:
+- A9 One or two questions per turn, in plain words, in the creator's language; no form (T).
+- A10 Before building it explains its method: how it researched, how it will build, what the app cannot do (T).
+- A11 At most 3 creator turns after the plan (T, counted, not self-reported).
+
+Content (S3, S6):
+- A12 The curriculum is clarified (Land, Schulform, Jahrgang, own material) and the competencies are written as
+  "Ich kann …" (P, T).
+- A13 `app-content` is filled in before building, from the confirmed method, and updated whenever a content decision
+  changes (G).
+- A14 Sources and licences of content by others are named (C: rubric).
+- A15 Texts for learners are German and in plain language (C: rubric).
+
+Platform rules (S1, `platform-rules.md`), the same for any way of building (E3):
+- A16 Static, browser only, no account, free, no ads, collects nothing, also after a click (C).
+- A17 WCAG 2.1 AA and usable at 360 px, or a declared and justified `limits` entry (C).
+- A18 Checkable: the published app can be opened and checked on its URL (`lernapps check <url>`) (C).
+
+Archetype (S2):
+- A19 It chooses the archetype that fits the learning goal and can say why; interactive only when the learner acts in
+  a way a quiz or an explainer cannot carry (T).
+- A20 Quiz: it writes only `src/quiz.json`. Explainer: content as YAML, components only where no block fits, readable
+  without JavaScript. Interactive: a pure deterministic core under the runtime (`start`, `step`, `tick`), playthroughs
+  that pass, storage through the wrapper within the quota, the architecture updated in the app sections (G, C).
+
+Checks and tooling (M1–M3):
+- A21 It acts on every check and hook message without asking the creator (T).
+- A22 It never bypasses a hook (`--no-verify`), never edits `prePushFailures`, never disables a check or a test, and
+  gives a reason for every suppression (G).
+- A23 Few failed pre-push runs: p90 of `prePushFailures` below 5 (P, written by the hook).
+- A24 `lernapps update` keeps its own app sections and skills; it never edits a `lernapps-*` skill (G).
+
+GitHub (S4, E5; cases from the Tipp-Huhn run, #18):
+- A25 The repo name is settled before the first push; `main` first as the default, then an empty `gh-pages`, then
+  `work` (G).
+- A26 The Pages source is `gh-pages`, set by the agent if it may, else by the creator's click at the exact place (G, T).
+- A27 Tools in the order of the skill (gh over REST, MCP, curl); a refusal by the integration becomes a click for the
+  creator, never a dummy push (T, G).
+- A28 It pushes only the branch the plan names; `main` only at publish, after the creator's yes (G, T).
+
+Listing (S5, M4, M5):
+- A29 It checks the listing criteria on the published app, not on its description (T).
+- A30 The entry is valid against the schema on the first try or after reading its messages (C).
+- A31 The pull request comes from a fork, branch `add-<id>`; nothing is pushed to lernapps/apps (G).
+- A32 It reads the results comment and fixes what it names; platform findings block, tooling findings are warnings
+  (T, G).
+
+Overall:
+- A33 Time from the first prompt to an entry ready to list, for the MVP assumption `a-creators-list` (T).
+- A34 Where it had to guess: every guess is written in the retrospective and becomes a finding for the guidance
+  (P, KD-12).
+
+#### 3. What we expect of the review agent (R1)
+- B1 It reviews exactly the named commit on `main`, starting from the validation report (C).
+- B2 It judges each rubric item with evidence, separates platform rules (blocking) from tooling rules (warnings), and
+  changes nothing (C).
+- B3 Its verdict on seeded apps (one that passes, one with a hidden platform violation, one built freely without our
+  tooling) matches the expected verdict.
+
 ### Sketch: the interactive archetype (step 12, decided by the owner)
 *From the owner's examples and answers, decided by the owner (2026-10-16).*

author: Claude
message:
feat(evals): the lernapps evals as Harbor tasks

Three single-step tasks with a fresh start (quiz-fresh, explainer-fresh,
interactive-fresh): the creator's first message is the build prompt E1
exactly as lernapps.net/apps/build/ renders it, and a simulated creator
plays a German teacher persona per archetype over ACP until the publish
or listing checkpoint. The image is the creator's machine: Node 22, git
and Chromium for `lernapps check`, an empty /app.

A separate verifier scores the collected /app (evals/verifier/verify.ts,
numbers only, with evidence lines): plan and front matter against the
schema of the tooling the app installed, archetype, phase, ticked boxes,
retrospective, "Ich kann", content guide, app created, `lernapps check`
after `npm ci`, committed and clean, prePushFailures.
evals/score-transcript.ts scores the agent's session log: creator turns
after the plan, questions per turn, approvals after a question, guidance
read raw or through a summarising fetch, reads outside the guidance,
installs before the plan, hook bypasses, and the agent's own tokens
(Harbor's numbers for an ACP target are not the target's).
evals/summary.ts aggregates jobs per task and configuration and never
mixes configurations; evals/expectations.json maps each dimension to its
expectation.

evals/harbor/: setup.sh installs Harbor 0.24.0 outside the repo, applies
two patches (the subscription token for the ACP adapter; the acpx config
in ~/.acpx instead of .acpxrc.json in the workspace, which made
`lernapps create` refuse /app in the first real run) and writes the
generated files of the tasks (egress CA, verifier, schema; gitignored).
harbor.sh runs Harbor with a scrubbed environment; run.sh runs one job
per task and model and writes its configuration.json.

Tests: the transcript score on a synthetic trial and on a trimmed
recorded trial, the verifier's plan parsing, the summary.

message:
feat(evals): score the skills loaded in their phase (A2), from the architecture

A trial now also scores whether the agent loads the skills its guidance names for a phase in that phase, in full:
`skills_in_phase` (the share of expected skills loaded within the phase, from the call that sets it in the plan to
the one that sets the next) and `skills_out_of_place` (a skill of another archetype, or one loaded before its
phase). What is expected comes from the `x-phase` of the skills' building blocks in the architecture at the job's
guidance commit: `evals/skills-by-phase.ts`, written into the job by `run.sh`. Each task names the skills it leaves
to a condition (`skills_conditional` in `task.toml`). Jobs without it, like the runs of 2026-10-18, keep their
scores; the report shows the two rows empty for them.

A read of `SKILL.md` after `cd` into the skill's folder counts as a load too.

author: Claude
message:
feat(evals): one results file per eval run, cleaned of trials that are no results; skills loaded by their phase's end

`evals/results.ts` writes `evals/runs/<run>/results.json` (schema results.v1) from the jobs of one eval run. The file
holds the configurations (a run may hold several, never mixed), a cell per task, model and configuration with n,
mean, min and max of every row and metric, every trial with its numbers and status, and the jobs left out with
their reason and the job that replaced them. Left out: a job with excluded.txt, a trial that hit the subscription's
usage limit (the API's own error names in its logs) or broke off before its agent started. A trial whose verifier
crashed stays a result without the verifier's numbers ("partial"). No transcripts, no paths, no credentials.

The run of 2026-10-18 is the first such file; its cells equal the page's data.json.

The skill score (A2) now counts a skill as loaded when it was loaded by the end of its phase; loading it before its
phase counts once, as out of place, instead of twice.

- An example bank in German (fractions, grade 5 and 6) with one question of each of the six types, so the creator's
  assistant sees every type before it replaces the questions.
- `@lernapps/tooling` pinned to a commit with a lockfile, so the folder can be tried on its own (`npm ci`) and
  `npm ci` works in the generated app; the generator renames the package after the app's folder.
- `build` writes `_site/` for the site actions; `check` is `lernapps check`.
- A workflow checks every template folder with `lernapps check`.

## Side effects
- The README describes the repo as the templates of the archetypes instead of an empty single template.

author: Claude
message:
feat(quiz): the quiz runtime as the package @lernapps/app-templates, a knowledge quiz

## Intent
Apps depend on their archetype's runtime as a package, so a new feature (a timer, a question type) reaches an app
with a dependency bump. And quizzes are mostly about things to know: every option carries short background
knowledge, every question links to further reading.

## Key decisions
- The repo root is the package `@lernapps/app-templates`, installed from git at a commit (npm cannot install a
  subfolder). Exports per archetype: `quiz` (engine), `quiz/plugin` (the Vite build step: validate and render),
  `quiz/style.css`, `quiz/e2e` (generic Playwright tests), the schema. `files` ships only `dist/` and `runtime/`;
  `prepare` builds `dist/` with vp pack.
- `@lernapps/tooling` and Playwright are optional peer dependencies: every app has them, and installing the runtime
  from git then needs nothing from GitHub besides this repo. The root's own type check installs tooling without
  saving it (CI job `runtime`).
- The template uses the runtime of its own commit (`file:..`, installed as a copy through `.npmrc`, so app and
  runtime share one Playwright). Its `vite.config.ts` composes the two: `lernapps({ plugins: [quiz()] })`. It pins
  `@lernapps/tooling` to main (the shared preset).
- Question bank: options have `text`, `correct`, `info` (background on the option itself, true either way) and an
  optional `link`; questions have `explanation` and at least one link in `links`; the quiz has optional `sources`.
  Per-option `feedback` is gone: `info` plus the marking of the right option and the learner's choice say the same
  without a second text that can contradict it. True/false, number, ordering and matching carry their background
  in `explanation`. The schema stays v1: it was never published.
- After an answer the page shows every option's background, the right ones and the learner's choice marked, the
  explanation and the links; the worksheet without JavaScript shows the same in its answer key. Links to other sites
  are plain links with rel="noopener", as in the site frame.
- Example bank "Naturwunder der Welt": eight questions of all six types, written in my own words from the German
  Wikipedia articles they link (each checked: HTTP 200, no disambiguation page).
- The unit tests of the scoring move here with the code.

## Side effects
- The bank's `$schema` points into node_modules, so the editor validates against the installed version.
- The template has no lockfile: the generator rewrites the runtime dependency, and the app's first `npm install`
  writes its lockfile.

The content is YAML in src/: app.yaml with its languages and the order of the
chapters, a folder per chapter with chapter.yaml and its pages, data/ and

definitions, one hidden chapter kept in the address, a page tree per language
with lang, hreflang and a language switch without JavaScript, llms.txt per tree
and the archetype marker. Language maps live in runtime/shared/languages.ts, for
the quiz's question blocks to reuse.

highlight.js 11.12.0 (BSD-3-Clause), yaml 2.9.1 (ISC).

author: Claude
message:
feat(explainer): explicit {{placeholders}} in generated exercises, checked at build

A placeholder of a generated exercise is now always two braces around a declared name or its field, nothing else
inside: {{G}}, {{e.name}}, {{answer}}, in prose and in formulas alike. One brace is never a placeholder, so a bare
letter is always the letter: in a formula G, {G} and \frac{W}{G} stay letters, with no spaces needed to keep a
declared name from being filled in. One brace cannot carry placeholders inside formulas, as it is LaTeX grouping
(\frac{W}{G} reads both ways); two braces around a lone name are the only LaTeX form this reserves, and that form
means the same as the name alone, so nothing is lost. Where a formula needs a group around a value, the group stays:
\frac{{{W}}}{{{G}}}.

The build fails, naming the file, its line, the block path, the language and the placeholder:
- on a placeholder whose name given does not declare (nor answer; figure.… in the figure's alt);
- in prose, on a declared name with one pair of braces ({G}), and anywhere on two braces with spaces inside ({{ G }});
- on a variable of given used by no placeholder and no expression of the figure, the answer (with a choice's or a
  set's options) or the mistakes; where does not count;
- as before, on a placeholder left after filling in, now also in the figure's alt.

The Prozent pages, the fixtures, the default alt texts and the schema's descriptions use the new syntax; the broken
fixture has a case each for an unknown placeholder, one brace and an unused variable.

message:
feat(explainer): vue-component blocks, rendered at build and hydrated as islands

A vue-component block names a component of src/components/<Name>.vue, gives its props and requires a nojs text
(restricted Markdown, by language), which the page shows in place without JavaScript.

- The build renders each block's component with Vue's server renderer in each language into its island, hidden until
  it hydrates; it then replaces the nojs text, or keeps it as its caption with defineOptions({ nojs: "caption" }).
  Only pages with a component load the islands module, and with it Vue; each component is a chunk of its own. An app
  without components loads nothing of Vue at build either: @vitejs/plugin-vue and the SFC compiler load only then.
- Each block's props are checked against the component's prop types (defineProps<…>()), resolved by Vue's SFC
  compiler; a string prop is a learner text, checked for every declared language and given in the page's language.
- On the SFC compiler's output (script and compiled template, mapped back to the .vue file) and the modules of the
  folder: no network, no eval, new Function, innerHTML or v-html, imports only from vue, this runtime,
  @lernapps/tooling/storage, i18n and a11y and the folder, browser globals only inside onMounted (and the unmount
  hooks); a test file per component; 20 kB gzip of a component's own code. One line per problem, with file and place.
- A component that emits answered is an exercise: its logic module <Name>.ts exports generate(seed, props),
  check(task, answer), solution(task) and wrong(task), property-tested over 50 fixed seeds per block; answered drives
  the quiz's feedback below the island.
- explainerTests(): without JavaScript each component's nojs text is visible and not empty; with JavaScript, in
  German at 360 px, each component hydrates without a console error, and an exercise's answered gives the feedback.
- The history fixture gets its component, AssignLabels, a pyramid whose levels the learner labels, with its logic
  module and test; the broken cases are build-only unit tests. vue 3.5.43 and @vitejs/plugin-vue 6.0.9 pinned;
  vue-tsc type-checks the fixtures' .vue files at the root (npm run check:vue, in CI).

every file it lints and reports only the app's own files.

PropType now live in content.ts, so what src/ reaches needs no Node.

Task numbers now name distinct tasks: the build walks the seeds 1, 2, 3, … through an exercise's generator (generated
and exercise components alike) and keeps each seed whose task differs from every earlier one (a generated exercise's

message:
docs: one architecture for every archetype, generic at the repo root with an extension per archetype

The architecture of interactive apps becomes the generic architecture of every lernapps app in docs/arc42/: the
frame (static description, page trees, 404 page, build checks, shell, end-to-end tests, tooling helpers, the
optional tutor handoff, task numbers, exercise contract, settings, loading indicator) and an abstract archetype part.
quiz/, explainer/ and interactive/ each get an extension in docs/arc42/ with only the blocks, interfaces,
decisions, risks and terms their archetype adds below the generic ones. Readable without JavaScript is a quality

author: Claude
message:
chore(skills): install the commit skill from mrsimpson/skills-coding

## Intent

Most commits of the agentic app-creation increment say what changed but not why; the intent stayed in the
sessions and was lost. Agents working in this repo now load a commit skill that asks for it in every message.

## Key changes

- Every commit message gets a conventional subject and a body with "Intent", "Key changes" and, where it applies,
  "Dependencies and side effects".
- The skill is installed with `npx skills add mrsimpson/skills-coding -s commit` and pinned in `skills-lock.json`;
  `.claude/skills/commit` links it for Claude Code.

## Dependencies and side effects

The same skill is installed in every platform repository of lernapps, so all of them share one commit format.

The pre-push hook counts `.agents/`, `.claude/` and `skills-lock.json` as root-only paths: no template's check needs them.

message:
feat: first draft of the app overview (find, app page, list an app)

## Intent

The application of lernapps.net for the first-draft MVP of the platform
design (D8 mvp-first-draft), built from its experiences (D7): a teacher
finds an app minutes before a lesson, sees at a glance that it may be
used, brings it to class and says thanks; a parent does the same the
evening before a test; a creator lists an app in minutes and hears back.

## Key decisions

- Static pages with Eleventy and UnoCSS, as on the home page: every page
  works without JavaScript, every app has a real page for deep and
  referral links.
- Reusable parts as Nunjucks macros (components.njk); texts in de.js,
  plain German (ISO 24495-1), "du".
- One YAML entry per app; the build checks it and renders the QR code.
- Thanks, use, feedback and referral clicks post to a configurable
  counter; while there is none, the block steps aside quietly.
- Privacy notice and imprint linked on every page, checked in CI.
- First entries: the three apps of the Mathe-Karte.

message:
feat(listing): every finding as a task; explicit cutoff only past GitHub's limit

## Intent

The listing results comment showed at most 50 findings in rule order and
then "… und N weitere Befunde": rules whose findings all fell past the cap
never appeared (in a test run, all 14 usable-at-360px findings). Now every
finding is a task (`- [ ]`), grouped by rule, so every rule is visible.

## Key decisions

- Each task: the rule id linked to its rule page and the severity; where,
  found and fix stay in a fenced code block, as before, because the reports
  are data from the pull request.
- Only a comment above 60,000 bytes (GitHub takes 65,536 characters) is cut
  off. Then it says how many findings it shows of how many, lists every rule
  with its count and how many are shown, shows the same number of findings of
  every rule (the largest that fits), and links the full report: the artifact
  `listing` of the run (its address, looked up by listing-comment.yml), else
  the run.
- The comment is rewritten on every run, so ticked boxes start empty again.

author: Claude
message:
feat(eintragen): the creator's entry point to building an app

## Intent

A creator should get from lernapps.net to a generated app without reading a
repo (lernapps/tooling#21). /apps/eintragen/ only listed apps that already
exist; it now starts with "Noch keine App?": a prompt to give the assistant,
the command that starts the app, the skill lernapps-app as the quick path,
and a link on to listing. llms.txt has the same as "Eine App bauen", before
"Eine App eintragen".

## Key decisions

- Test first, end to end (test/entry-point.e2e.test.mjs): the site is built,
  every link on the page and in llms.txt resolves (into the build or on the
  web), and the command is taken from the built page, run in an empty folder
  for every archetype the tooling at that ref names, followed by git init,
  npm install and `npx lernapps check`, which must pass.
- The command is the plan template's: `npx --yes github:lernapps/tooling#main
  create --archetype <archetype>`, without a folder argument, so it writes
  into the folder that holds the plan. Nothing is installed globally.
- The prompt asks the assistant to read the tooling's llms.txt, follow the
  quick path, and generate only after the plan is confirmed
  (explore-before-code). The page names no entry fields and no rules; the
  skill, the plan and the schema explain themselves.
- Command, skill and llms.txt links are settings in src/_data/site.js, one
  source for the page and llms.txt.

## Side effects (if any)

npm test now needs the network (github.com, codeload.github.com, the npm
registry, lernapps.net) and takes about a minute longer.

author: Claude
message:
feat(build,enter): building and listing on their own pages, English paths

## Intent

The owner's review of step 13: building an app and listing a published one
are two different jobs, so they get two pages, /apps/build/ and /apps/enter/,
with English paths and German texts. /apps/eintragen/ is gone, without a
redirect. The repo explains building and listing, and provides the apps
themselves; helping builders get their apps out is the tooling's job.

## Key decisions

- /apps/build/: the prompt for the assistant, the command, the skill
  lernapps-app as the quick path, then "Wie es weitergeht" with a link to
  the conditions and on to /apps/enter/. Nothing on it suggests the app
  exists already.
- /apps/enter/: listing a published app, as before, with one line for those
  without an app that leads to /apps/build/.
- de.js has separate texts for building (build) and listing (list); no
  string covers both. Listing texts speak of a published app; the index
  page and the app page link /enter/ for apps that are published.
- llms.txt: "Eine App bauen" and "Eine App eintragen" each link their page.
- The issue form is renamed app-enter.yml, so no URL holds the old path.
- @lernapps/site is pinned to lernapps/lernapps.github.io#25, whose
  navigation links /apps/build/ and /apps/enter/; without it the
  navigation would link a page that no longer exists.
- Tests follow: every link on /apps/build/, /apps/enter/ and llms.txt
  resolves; the command is taken from /apps/build/ and gives an app that
  passes lernapps check.

## Side effects (if any)

Links to /apps/eintragen/ elsewhere break; the other repos are updated in
their own pull requests. The @lernapps/site pin moves to main once
lernapps.github.io#25 is merged.

message:
feat(review): a maintainer's /review runs the review agent on a listing pull request

A comment `/review` (or `/review <commit>`) by a member who can write to the repo starts .github/workflows/review.yml:

- input (no secret, read-only token): reads the request and the entry, builds the app at the commit in a container
  and runs `lernapps check <bundle> --entry --report` (scripts/review-input.mjs); uploads what the agent reads;
- review (the secret, a token that can only read): lernapps/tooling at main as the working directory, the input next
  to it as data, claude-code-action with Read, Glob, Grep and Write for the verdict file only; it runs only when the
  checks report no error; tooling's verdict check validates the verdict;
- comment (writes the comment, no secret, no agent): scripts/review-comment.mjs renders the verdict, or why there is
  none, into one comment marked `<!-- lernapps-review -->`, rewritten on every review.

The listing comment and llms.txt no longer promise a review: lernapps.net decides, and may review first. The README
tells maintainers about /review.

npm ci sets core.hooksPath to .githooks/ (the prepare script); this repo has no vite-plus, so no vp config. Both

  the review build in its container needs Docker.
- test/pre-push.test.mjs: TOOLING_REF is the commit of changes.yml@ and tooling-ref in every workflow and of the

author: Claude
message:
test(entry-point): an outside host's passing 5xx or 429 is a note; the archetypes run at the same time

The link checks fetch with test/links.mjs. Our own hosts (lernapps.net and its subdomains) stay strict: any answer
but 2xx after redirects fails, never retried. An outside host that answers 5xx or 429 is asked again after 2 s and
after 5 s; if it still does, the test writes a note into its output (a diagnostic) instead of failing: main's Pages
run failed on github.com/lernapps/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md answering 503. Any other answer of an outside
host (404, ...) and a failed fetch still fail. test/links.test.mjs tests the classification against a local server
(503 and 429 retried three times, then a note; 404 broken at once; our own host strict; the waits); the pre-push
hook runs it with the other offline tests.

The archetype test ("run in an empty folder ... for every archetype") runs the archetypes at the same time, each in
its own folder, with its own preview port (LERNAPPS_PREVIEW_PORT, which the tooling's Playwright configuration
takes; the ports are chosen together, so they differ) and its share of the cores as Playwright workers
(LERNAPPS_PLAYWRIGHT_WORKERS). One after the other it took 89 to 128 s in CI's last four runs.

## Intent

Teachers asked who stands behind the privacy of an app that lives at its creator's own address, and developers asked for feedback that reaches them directly.

## Key changes

- Fitness note: "Die App wurde geprüft: Bei der Aufnahme hat eine automatische Prüfung diese Angaben mit der App verglichen."
- An app outside lernapps.net gets a second note: it is on an external site (the host is named); lernapps.net cannot take responsibility for privacy there; whoever has concerns can ask the provider whether they would like to host the app on lernapps.net, with a link to the creator.
- Feedback: for an app whose source is on GitHub, "Du hast ein GitHub-Konto? Dann schreib es direkt an <creator>: Issue anlegen" opens a new issue in the app's repository, with the title and the app's address filled in.

+# Development Plan: apps (feat/serve-copies branch)
+
+*Generated on 2026-10-21 by Vibe Feature MCP*
+*Workflow: [epcc](https://codemcp.github.io/workflows/workflows/epcc)*
+
+## Goal
+
+lernapps.net serves a copy of every listed app (lernapps/docs KD-21, lernapps/apps#58), our own apps included: one address, one privacy notice, links that keep working. When a listing pull request is merged, and on every update of an entry, the app is built from the commit its entry names and published at `https://lernapps.net/<id>/`. The creator stays the author and keeps the repo, the licence and their own address.
+
+Repos involved: lernapps/apps (entries, building the copies), lernapps/lernapps.github.io (the root site that serves `/<id>/`), lernapps/tooling (rule `own-data-only`, the site and publish actions, arc42), the app repos of the lernapps organisation (their own Pages switched off once the copy is live).
+
+## Key Decisions
+
+### KD-01: Copies at `lernapps.net/<id>/`, served by the root site (2026-10-21)
+`/apps/<id>/app/` would put "app" three times into the address teachers type or scan. `/<id>/` is the shortest, and our four apps in the organisation keep their address exactly, so links on worksheets do not break (#57).
+- **Decision**: The copies are part of the root site (lernapps.github.io), each under `/<id>/`. Not one repo per app: that needs a GitHub App that creates repos.
+- **Consequence**: ids must not collide with paths of the root site or with other repos served below lernapps.net (`apps`, `docs`, `tooling`, `en`, …): a list of reserved ids, checked by the listing validation.
+- **Consequence**: the 1 GB limit of GitHub Pages is shared by the home page and all copies; enough for small learning apps.
+
+### KD-02: Our own apps are built and published the same way (2026-10-21)
+No exception for the apps in the organisation: they get an entry `commit` and a copy like every other app. Once the copy is live, the app repo's own Pages is switched off, so the copy takes over the same address.
+
+### KD-03: The copy is the bundle built from the entry's pinned commit (2026-10-21)
+The entry gets a required field `commit` (full id). The copy is built from that commit with `scripts/review-input.mjs` (the review's build: clone, `npm ci && npm run build` or the repo as its own bundle, in a container, without secrets) and checked with `lernapps check <bundle> --entry`. What is served is what was checked, not what happens to be at the creator's address. `url` stays the creator's address, which the listing check of a pull request opens.
+
+### KD-04: Copies built in apps, published by the root site (2026-10-21)
+- apps, on a push to `main` that changes `entries/*.yaml`: a job without secrets and with a read-only token builds the changed entries in a container; a job with `contents: write` (normal `GITHUB_TOKEN`, runs no app code) writes the bundles to the branch `copies` of lernapps/apps, one directory per id; a deleted entry removes its directory.
+- lernapps.github.io: its Pages deploy checks out `apps@copies` and puts each directory under `_site/<id>/` after the site's own build and check, so home page and copies go online together.
+
+### KD-05: An app touches only its own data (2026-10-20, lernapps/tooling branch feat/own-data-only)
+All copies share the origin lernapps.net with each other and the platform. Rule `own-data-only`, scope listing, severity error: keys, databases and caches named `lernapps:<id>:`, `<id>` the catalog id.
+
+### KD-06: Relative paths are a condition for listing (2026-10-21)
+Checked: all seven listed apps reference their files relatively (`./assets/…`); apps built with the tooling use `base: "./"` (archetypes/shared/preset.ts). The check of the copy at its new path catches an app with fixed paths; no separate rule.
+
+## Notes
+
+### Open questions (decide in Explore)
+1. **Trigger of the root site's deploy.** A workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` only works in its own repo, so apps cannot start the deploy of lernapps.github.io without a credential. Options: (a) a GitHub App of the organisation with only *Actions: write* on lernapps.github.io; a small job in apps that runs no app code mints a short-lived token and runs `gh workflow run`. (b) a fine-grained personal access token (bound to a person, expires). (c) no credential: a scheduled workflow in lernapps.github.io compares the head of `apps@copies` with the deployed one, every 15 minutes (up to 15 minutes delay; GitHub pauses schedules after 60 days without activity).
+2. **Updates: review or automatic?** Every update of an app goes the same way (new `commit` by pull request, check, merge, build, deploy). Proposal: an update is merged automatically when the listing check is green; a review only for a first listing and when the licence or the source repo changes; a scheduled workflow opens the update pull request when the creator's `main` moves. With that, the trigger matters, so option (a).
+
+### Facts found
+- review.yml today reviews the head of the app repo's `main` or `/review <commit>`; with the pinned commit it should default to the entry's `commit`.
+- tooling's `site-deploy` replaces `gh-pages` and only keeps `pr-preview/` (`clean-exclude`); the copies must therefore be part of the site artifact, not written to `gh-pages` beside it.
+- Catalog (src/_data/catalog.js): `app.url`, the topic links and the QR code are built from `entry.url`; they move to `https://lernapps.net/<id>/`.
+- Of the listed apps, only mathe-karte fails `own-data-only` (keys without prefix, e.g. `binom-trainer.selbsteinschaetzung`, `dtc-theme`); same origin as before, so learners' progress can be migrated in the app.
+- To verify: a repo with Pages in the organisation (e.g. lernapps/mathe-karte) shadows the root site's `/<id>/`, so the copy takes over only after that repo's Pages is switched off.
+
+## Explore
+### Phase Entrance Criteria
+- The need is stated: lernapps/apps#58, lernapps/docs KD-21.
+
+### Tasks
+- [ ] Decide the trigger of the root site's deploy (open question 1)
+- [ ] Decide the update policy (open question 2)
+- [ ] Verify that a project repo's Pages shadows the root site's `/<id>/`, and what happens when it is switched off
+- [ ] Build all seven apps at their current commits with `review-input.mjs` and check the bundles (sizes, relative paths)
+- [ ] List the reserved ids (paths of the root site, repos served below lernapps.net)
+
+### Completed
+- [x] Created development plan file
+- [x] Path decided: `lernapps.net/<id>/` (KD-01), own apps included (KD-02)
+- [x] Rule `own-data-only` built in tooling (KD-05)
+- [x] Relative paths of the listed apps checked (KD-06)
+
+## Plan
+### Phase Entrance Criteria
+- Open questions 1 and 2 are decided.
+- The shadowing of `/<id>/` by project repos is verified.
+- All seven apps build at a pinned commit.
+
+### Tasks

+- The user approved the plan.

+### KD-04: Four steps from an entry to its copy (2026-10-21)
+The steps are described under "Steps" below: build the app, push it into its subdirectory of `gh-pages`, start it automatically, take over the apps already listed. This replaces the earlier idea of a branch `copies` in lernapps/apps that the root site's deploy pulls in: the copy goes straight into the `gh-pages` branch that serves `lernapps.net/<id>/`, and GitHub Pages publishes it on that push.
 
 ### KD-05: An app touches only its own data (2026-10-20, lernapps/tooling branch feat/own-data-only)
 All copies share the origin lernapps.net with each other and the platform. Rule `own-data-only`, scope listing, severity error: keys, databases and caches named `lernapps:<id>:`, `<id>` the catalog id.
@@ -33,10 +32,43 @@ All copies share the origin lernapps.net with each other and the platform. Rule
 ### KD-06: Relative paths are a condition for listing (2026-10-21)
 Checked: all seven listed apps reference their files relatively (`./assets/…`); apps built with the tooling use `base: "./"` (archetypes/shared/preset.ts). The check of the copy at its new path catches an app with fixed paths; no separate rule.
 
+## Steps
+
+### 1. Build the app
+- Where: a workflow in lernapps/apps (`publish.yml`), job `build`: no secrets, a read-only token, the build in a container (`BUILD_IMAGE` as in review.yml).
+- What: for each added or changed entry, `scripts/review-input.mjs --repo <source> --commit <commit> --container <image>`: clone at the pinned commit, `npm ci && npm run build` (or the repo as its own bundle), `lernapps check <bundle> --entry`.
+- Result: the bundle as an artifact (`copy-<id>`), without symbolic links, `.git`, `node_modules` and top-level dotfiles; only when the check reports no error. An entry whose build or check fails is not published, its copy stays as it was, and the run fails visibly.
+- Needs: the required fields `source` (a GitHub repo) and `commit` (a full id) in `schemas/entry.js`; review.yml reviews the entry's `commit` by default.
+
+### 2. Push into its subdirectory of `gh-pages`
+- Where: job `publish` in the same workflow; it downloads the artifacts and runs no app code.
+- What: writes each bundle to `<id>/` of the `gh-pages` branch of lernapps/lernapps.github.io (the root site that serves `lernapps.net/<id>/`), replacing that directory only, in one commit "copy of `<source>@<commit>`". A deleted entry removes its directory. GitHub Pages publishes the branch on that push: no extra deploy needed.
+- Then: `lernapps check https://lernapps.net/<id>/ --entry` against the copy (job `verify`), after Pages has deployed.
+- Needs:
+  - A credential that may push to lernapps.github.io: a GitHub App of the organisation with only *Contents: write* on that repo (preferred: no person, no expiry), or a fine-grained token. Only the job `publish` gets it.
+  - tooling's `site-deploy` must keep the copies when the home page deploys: today it only keeps `pr-preview/` (`clean-exclude`). Proposal: `publish` maintains a list of the copies in `gh-pages` (e.g. `copies.txt`, one id per line), and `site-deploy` takes `clean-exclude` from it.
+  - Reserved ids: no copy may overwrite a path of the home page (`en/`, `assets/`, …) or a repo served below lernapps.net (`apps`, `docs`, `tooling`, …); the listing validation rejects them.
+
+### 3. Start it automatically
+- First listing: the merge of the listing pull request (push to `main` changing `entries/*.yaml`) starts `publish.yml`.
+- Update: a scheduled workflow in lernapps/apps compares each entry's `commit` with the head of `main` of its `source` and opens (or updates) one pull request per app that sets the new `commit`; the listing check runs on it as on every entry change. Merged automatically when the check is green, unless the licence or the source repo changed (open question 2); its merge starts `publish.yml` like a listing.
+- Delisting: a merged pull request that deletes the entry starts `publish.yml`, which removes the copy.
+- By hand: `workflow_dispatch` with an id rebuilds one copy, e.g. after a failed run.
+
+### 4. The apps already listed
+| App | Source | Address today | What changes |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| anorganische-chemie, elektrizitaet, naturwunder-quiz | lernapps | `lernapps.net/<id>/` from its own repo's Pages | Copy at the same address; then switch off the repo's Pages and its publish workflow, so the root site serves `/<id>/` (to verify: a repo's Pages shadows the root site's path) |
+| mathe-karte | lernapps | `lernapps.net/mathe-karte/` | As above; before that: keys with the prefix `lernapps:mathe-karte:`, migrating the old ones (`own-data-only`), and a licence file (none found) |
+| kniffel-trainer, textcheck, typonaut | mrsimpson | `mrsimpson.github.io/<id>/` | New address `lernapps.net/<id>/` in the catalog; the creator's address stays as it is |
+- Each entry gets `commit` (the current head of `main`) in one pull request; its merge builds and publishes all seven copies.
+- Order for the four apps of the organisation: copy published and checked, then their Pages switched off, so the address never breaks.
+- The licences: six apps are MIT, but their copyright line names "Claude", not the creator; to fix in the app repos (the creator holds the rights). mathe-karte has no licence file.
+
 ## Notes
 
 ### Open questions (decide in Explore)
-1. **Trigger of the root site's deploy.** A workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` only works in its own repo, so apps cannot start the deploy of lernapps.github.io without a credential. Options: (a) a GitHub App of the organisation with only *Actions: write* on lernapps.github.io; a small job in apps that runs no app code mints a short-lived token and runs `gh workflow run`. (b) a fine-grained personal access token (bound to a person, expires). (c) no credential: a scheduled workflow in lernapps.github.io compares the head of `apps@copies` with the deployed one, every 15 minutes (up to 15 minutes delay; GitHub pauses schedules after 60 days without activity).
+1. **Credential for the push to lernapps.github.io (step 2).** A workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` only works in its own repo. lernapps.net serves a copy of every listed app, ours included (lernapps/docs
KD-21, #58; plan .vibe/development-plan-feat-serve-copies.md).

- Entry format: `source` (a GitHub repo) and `commit` (a full id) required;
  the seven entries pinned to the head of their main. Reserved ids: no path
  of the home page, no other repo of the organisation (schemas/reserved.js).

  commit in a container without secrets, checks it, pushes the copy into
  <id>/ of the root site's gh-pages with the organisation's GitHub App
  (environment publish), keeps copies.txt, checks the copy where it is
  served and builds the catalog again.
- Catalog: links an app's copy only when copies.txt lists it at the entry's
  commit; otherwise the entry's url.
- update.yml: daily pull requests update/<id> for apps whose main moved;
  merged automatically only when nothing but versions of existing npm
  dependencies changed (scripts/update-kind.mjs), else labelled review.
- /review reviews the entry's commit by default.
- Texts: the licence must allow the copy; the creator stays the author.

Needs before the merge: lernapps/tooling's site-deploy that keeps the
copies (feat/copies-served), pinned in lernapps/lernapps.github.io.

author: Claude
message:
feat: tell the platform's story on the home page

## Intent

The home page still told the edugo story: school leadership as a
persona, the capability map at the centre, "be found" as the promise to
people who build apps, contributions by pull request. The platform
design has moved on, and people who might build apps need to see
plainly how the platform works and why it can be free. Many will think
"that doesn't work anyway".

## Key decisions

- Personas: teacher (minutes before a lesson), parent (the evening
  before a test), people who build apps (for their own class or child),
  learner; one quote and one portrait each, same tab mechanics.
- New sections: the principles (free, apps keep input on the device,
  open counting instead of tracking, thanks keeps it alive, a note for
  data protection officers); why it is free, with a personal word by
  the platform owner; an honest answer for sceptics linking to the
  rendered platform design, its MVP chapter and the vision.
- The capability map mock-up and the three "how it works" steps are
  gone; nav and footer link the platform design.
- Plain German after ISO 24495-1, in the tone of the old page.
- Hero headline: capped size and a soft hyphen, so it no longer
  overflows on desktop or breaks mid-word on phones.

## Side effects

- /docs/platform-design/ is linked; it is served by lernapps/docs.
- README describes the new story and points to the pdt skill.

  the commit of changes.yml@ and tooling-ref in every workflow; a push of only the plan checks nothing.

author: Claude
message:
feat: home page tells a solution-first story; new features and about pages

## Intent

Feedback: the home page spoke to neither parents nor teachers. It opened with a problem and reached the solution only in its third section. Now it starts with the promise and tells one story, with the passion of parents and teachers as its thread.

## Key changes

- Home page: "Lern-Apps ohne Haken." with four badges; four apps from the catalog; what teachers (a covering lesson) and parents (practise tonight, with the AI tutor of the explainer apps) get; "Ein solides Fundament für Macher"; "Noch eine Plattform?" answered with "diese gehört keiner Firma"; how to join; a short word from the founder. The persona tabs, the problem quotes and the ask-your-assistant box go, and with them start.js and start.css.
- /features/: the principles, what the apps can do (the three foundations, curriculum, feedback, deep links, AI tutor, accessibility), and technical transparency for developers: why it works without money, how an app gets into the catalog, stack, ownership and licence.
- /about/: the founder's long text (digital education has an ecosystem problem, not a device problem) and the answer for sceptics, moved from the home page.
- English translation of all three pages; README and llms.txt name the new pages.

## Dependencies and side effects

The home page has no script any more. "Gebaut von" is not shown on the app cards, so the home page names the founder once.

## Intent

Second round of persona feedback: parents and teachers asked who vouches for the content, stumbled over the AI tutor and over the makers' half of the home page; developers asked who decides on listing.

- Quality, honestly: every app comes from a person; we help them build it, but that is no guarantee. Mistakes in the content are reported on the app's page ("Fehler im Inhalt", lernapps/apps). On the home page under the examples, and on /features/ as "Von Menschen gemacht".

- /features/: anyone can submit an app; it is checked against the rules for every app, which are exclusion criteria. The operator no longer appears as the one who decides. The thank-you is explained as it is today: a prepared email that lernapps.net passes on.

author: Claude
message:
feat(site-frame): the browser's language until the reader chooses, and a line where a page falls back

On every page with a language switch, a small inline script goes to the
same page in the language the reader chose, else in their browser's (not
for crawlers). A choice by the switch is kept in localStorage only if it

+# Development Plan: lernapps.net platform design (feat/platform-design branch)
+
+*Started on 2026-09-29, following the [Platform Design Toolkit 2.2](https://docs.boundaryless.io/methodology/legacy/pdt) with the pdt42 CLI (`npx @pdt42/cli`)*
+
+## Goal
+
+Design lernapps.net as a platform with the Platform Design Toolkit: find where the platform opportunity lies (Exploration), design the platform for its ecosystem (Strategy Design), then plan launch and growth (Growth). The model lives in `docs/pdt42/` and is written in English; `pdt42 guide` and `pdt42 validate` are the source of truth for the status.
+
+---
+
+## Key Decisions
+
+### KD-01: Ecosystem is small, active-learning educational apps (E1)
+Apps with an explicit educational focus that make students active, each teaching one aspect. Value is created bottom-up today but does not compound: an app is built individually, used once, and rots.
+- **Decision**: Ministries, funding programmes and commissioned agencies are deliberately left out as actors. The top-down chain is why the ecosystem under-performs, not a route we act on.
+
+### KD-02: Four arenas in a pure sequence, focus on "Getting apps into use" (E1, E4)
+Spotting a need → Building the app → Getting apps into use → Evolving the app. No feedback loop from evolving to spotting, as gaps are usually whole apps.
+- **Decision**: "Getting apps into use" is the focus arena. Making an app available and using it are one arena, because the outcome only exists jointly.
+
+### KD-03: The ecosystem scan reflects the owners' own observations (E2)
+Eight entities, five jobs in the focus arena. Not yet validated with other ecosystem representatives; that students search via social media and AI assistants is an assumption.
+
+### KD-04: No asset is inimitable (E3)
+Modelling DSLs as agent guidance (vr, rare because we do not intend to earn money), frontend-only architecture (v), non-profit at near-zero marginal cost (vr).
+- **Decision**: The H002 hints stay open on purpose. The assets are supporting; the advantage has to come from the platform itself.
+
+### KD-05: The only moat is data protection law and terms of use (E3)
+Regulated, in the focus arena, without a holder. Teacher platforms are not a moat (alternative routes exist), and school gatekeepers can be bypassed by an entrepreneurial teacher.
+- **Decision**: Do not fight the moat; ease the interaction with it, e.g. through the frontend-only architecture.
+
+### KD-06: Three user needs on the Wardley Map (E5)
+Students understand the subject for good grades; parents want the same with little time; teachers gain free time by keeping students busy.
+- **Decision**: Evolution today: app custom, bringing to students product, discoverability custom, signal of fitness for use genesis; hosting, AI assistants, devices and connectivity commodity.
+
+---
+
+## Notes
+
+- Exploration is optional in the PDT, but we do it to find the platformization space before designing.
+- `pdt42 next` points to D1, because the E2 entities already count as started D1 work. We finish Exploration (E6, E7) first.
+- Preview: `pdt42 serve` only works locally; in a cloud session build with `pdt42 build --out <dir> --single-file`.
+
+---
+
+## Exploration
+
+### Tasks
+- [ ] E6 Apply the six Platform Plays (`:::play`, `component.target`)
+- [ ] E7 Identify the platformization space and consolidate the brief (`:::scenario`, `:::brief`)
+
+### Completed

+- [x] E4 Choose the arena to focus on

+## Strategy Design

+- [ ] D1 Map the ecosystem: give the eight entities a role, add the `:::platform` block and the Ecosystem Canvas (9 findings open)
+- [ ] D2 Portray the entity-roles

errors (EG03, wrong chapter), and ignore directives now accept one finding
each, so most accepted deviations resurfaced as hints. Migrate the model

  be ignored. E2 keeps its jobs and points to D1; the D1 lead-in now says it

  carry their kind's prefix (no WG08).

  before each of the three transactions without a channel (the shared
  reason split per transaction). H102 is reported at the sixth peer role,
  so its directive follows the D1 paragraph that explains the six roles.
  Rejected: stacking the directives at the top of the file, which would
  silently swallow an unrelated new finding of the same code above them.

author: Claude
message:
ci: render the platform design diff and comment it on pull requests

## Intent

The PR build skipped the platform design diff because pdt42 0.4.0 had no
`--diff`. With 0.6.1 reviewers can see what a PR changes in the platform
design, inside its chapters, without building it themselves.

## Key decisions

- `build.sh` with `PDT42_DIFF_BASE` renders `<base>...HEAD` (the change
  since the merge base, as pdt42's own platform-review workflow does) into
  `_site/platform-design-diff/` and writes `pdt42 diff --format json` as
  `changes.json`; diff findings are reported, not fatal. The skip guard is
  gone; without the variable nothing changes locally.
- The workflow passes the PR's base branch, uploads the single page also
  unzipped (`platform-design-review.html`, opens in the browser), and a
  separate `review-comment` job, the only one with `pull-requests: write`,
  posts one comment per PR (marker, updated in place, created only when the
  design changed; job summary only for forks), modelled on biz42's
  business-review workflow. `scripts/pdt42-review-summary.mjs` renders it.
- New actions pinned to commit SHAs: download-artifact v8.0.1,
  github-script v9.0.0.

## Side effects

- README describes the review artifacts and the comment.

ecosystem: whether supply comes about and whether thanks works as the

docs(pdt42): open counting instead of no tracking, platform as its own pitch

## Intent

Be precise about tracking: it means collecting data without the user's
knowledge. Counting single explicit interactions openly on the platform
is how the MVP learns whether valuable use happens. Trust is tested at
the moment of decision: does the platform convince teachers on its own?

## Key decisions

- KD-18 and the channels (D5): no hidden data collection; explicit
  clicks only, totals only, no cookies or browser storage, explained at
  the button; the apps collect nothing.
- Referral links carry one code per wave, never per person, and are not
  stored in the browser.
- First draft (D8): the teachers' experience takes part; new riskiest
  trust assumption "The platform convinces teachers on its own",
  tested by contacts forwarding a referral link to colleagues the owner
  does not know.
- Real MVP: teachers are reached through forwarding, with the platform
  as the pitch and a short letter, instead of separate material.

## Side effects

- H114 (first draft without trust assumption) resolved; three H115
  hints wait for the owner's values.
- Development plan: KD-18 rewritten, KD-19 and next actions updated.

-# Development Plan: edugo (feat/edugo-platform-research branch)
-
-*Generated on 2026-09-23 by Vibe Feature MCP*
-*Workflow: [greenfield](https://codemcp.github.io/workflows/workflows/greenfield)*
-
-## Goal
-
-Build the **infrastructure layer** that turns isolated educational micro-innovations into a coherent, trustworthy ecosystem — by mapping educational capabilities, ensuring lightweight quality standards, providing architecture guidelines for app builders, and making agentic creation ecosystem-connected. Delivered vaporware-first: a highly polished landing page, then frontend-only use cases on top of a GitHub-as-backend model.
-
----
-
-## Key Decisions
-
-### KD-01: Problem Anchor — PISA 2026 + Structural Failure (5 interlocking failures)
-1. "What children need" changes faster than institutions track
-2. Education depends on officially approved tools — slow pipeline
-3. Public authorities move on 3–5 year cycles (Digitalpakt = €11.5B, mostly infrastructure)
-4. Professional offerings are polished but passive and conservative
-5. Engaged individuals innovate but are isolated — work doesn't accumulate
-- **Decision**: edugo addresses all five. PISA 2026 is the narrative anchor; structural coordination is the actual problem.
-
-### KD-02: Second-Order Problem — Software Islands Without Coordination
-Cheap agentic engineering creates many micro-tools. Without coordination, these become disconnected islands whose capabilities can't be compared, whose quality can't be trusted, and that can't be extended. edugo's job is to prevent the island problem and build a coherent ecosystem instead.
-- **Decision**: edugo actively shapes the ecosystem via a capability map, quality standards, and architecture guidelines — not just a passive registry.
-
-### KD-03: Four Platform Jobs (not one)
-1. **Map capabilities** — living map of what should exist, what does exist, what's missing
-2. **Ensure essential quality** — lightweight standards (especially data safety) so data-sensitive users can trust community-built tools
-3. **Provide architecture guidelines** — patterns and scaffolding so new apps feel coherent and connected
-4. **Make agentic creation ecosystem-connected** — creation starts from a capability gap, uses edugo scaffolding, ends with a registry entry
-- **Decision**: All four jobs are in scope. The capability map is the strategic core; the others derive from it.
-
-### KD-04: Capability Map is the Strategic Core
-The capability map answers: "What educational capabilities do we need, and which currently exist?"
-- Nodes = discrete educational outcomes/activities
-- Status per node = Needed / Partially covered / Well covered
-- Linked solutions per node
-- Gap view = nodes with no/poor coverage surfaced as build opportunities
-- **Decision**: The capability map is the differentiator. It transforms edugo from a list into a strategy.
-
-### KD-05: Frontend-Only = DSGVO-Safe by Design
-An app with no backend has structurally no data exfiltration risk. edugo rewards this architecture with a visible "no backend — structurally DSGVO-safe" badge. This aligns product incentives with data safety: the easiest thing to build is also the safest thing.
-- **Decision**: Frontend-only architecture is first-class in the quality model. edugo's own infrastructure (Phase 1) is itself frontend-only.
-
-### KD-06: GitHub as Backend (Phase 1)
-- No server, no database — all data in structured files in this repo
-- Contribution = GitHub PR (naturally moderated, fully auditable, forkable)
-- Platform deployable from GitHub Pages
-- This models the exact architecture edugo recommends for apps
-- **Decision**: GitHub is the sole backend for Phase 1. This is a feature, not a constraint.
-
-### KD-07: Vaporware-First Delivery Strategy
-- **Phase 0**: Highly polished landing page. Tells the story, shows the concept visually, collects interest signals. Build the pitch before the product.
-- **Phase 1**: Frontend-only use cases on static infrastructure (capability map browse, registry view, client-side filter, GitHub PR contribution flow)
-- **Decision**: Ship Phase 0 first. Validate interest before building infrastructure.
-
-### KD-08: Active vs. Passive — Core Taxonomy
-Five levels: Create / Solve / Collaborate / Reflect / Receive.
-- **Decision**: Most prominent filter in discovery UI. First-class in data model.
-
-### KD-09: Progressive Trust Model
-Anecdotal → Community-validated → Research-backed. DSGVO shown honestly: green/amber/red/unknown. Frontend-only badge is automatic.
-- **Decision**: No editorial gatekeeping at submission; trust accumulates through use and evidence.
-
-### KD-10: Two Primary Users
-1. **Contributor (Builder)** — wants their work to reach others and be built upon
-2. **Adopter (Teacher)** — wants something safe, active-learning-focused, usable next Monday
-- **Decision**: Every product decision evaluated against both simultaneously.
-
-### KD-11: Open Questions
-- Who defines initial capability map nodes? (Most politically sensitive design choice)
-- Moderation at scale beyond a handful of PR reviewers?
-- Should edugo eventually host frontend-only apps as GitHub Pages sub-paths?
-- Sustainability: community organization model (like Serlo) needed eventually
-- Landing page CTA: email (DSGVO overhead) vs. GitHub star (frictionless but lossy)?
-- German-first content with English-native GitHub workflow — reconciliation?
-
----
-
-## Notes
-- The island problem is the new framing: cheap software creation without coordination = chaos. edugo coordinates.
-- "Frontend-only = DSGVO-safe" is a product insight that aligns incentives: easiest to build = safest to trust
-- GitHub-as-backend means the whole platform is itself a demonstration of the pattern it recommends
-- Vaporware-first is smart product strategy: generate signal before spending engineering time

-GitHub chosen because it has the largest contributor community and lowest onboarding friction — reach is the primary constraint in Phase 1. The underlying pattern is "Git-hosting provider as backend", not "GitHub specifically". The data layer (YAML+MD files under `data/`) must contain zero GitHub-specific markup. -## 1. Core Principles
-
-### 1.1 Data is the source of truth; code is a view over data
-
-Every capability node and every registry entry is a file. The Vue components, the capability map UI, and the trust signal badges are renderers — they have no business logic of their own that doesn't derive from reading and displaying data files. If a UI decision requires changing a data file structure, that is a data model change, not a UI change.
-
-**Defect signal:** if a component contains hard-coded capability IDs, trust thresholds, or taxonomy labels, something is wrong.
-
-### 1.2 The capability map is a graph; the UI is a projection of it
-
-The capability map data model is a directed graph (nodes with optional parent references). The UI offers multiple projections of this graph — tree view, domain view, gap view — but none of these projections change the underlying graph. A new projection is a new filter/render function, not a new data structure.
-
-**Defect signal:** if adding a new map view requires adding new fields to the capability node schema, something is wrong.
-
-### 1.3 Trust signals are computed, never editorial
-
-Trust signals (DSGVO status, evidence level, frontend-only badge) are derived mechanically from YAML frontmatter fields. There is no human editorial layer that overrides the computation. The only human action is writing a correct YAML field when submitting an entry.
-
-**Defect signal:** if a trust signal value is stored anywhere other than the source YAML file of the entry it describes, something is wrong.
-
-### 1.4 Client-side filtering is the only permitted query layer
-
-There is no server. Filtering and search operate on the full dataset loaded at page render time. The dataset must remain small enough (< 500KB uncompressed) for this to be fast. When the dataset grows beyond this limit, the solution is static pre-filtering at build time, not a server.
-
-**Defect signal:** if a component makes a network request to filter, search, or load registry entries at interaction time, something is wrong.
-
-### 1.5 Every user-visible text is in German; every identifier is in English
-
-Capability node titles, descriptions, and classroom scenarios are German. Component names, file names, YAML field keys, JSON Schema `$id` values, CSS class names, and git branch names are English. This separation is strict — it prevents the contribution workflow (GitHub-native, English) from mixing with the content (German-first).
-
-**Defect signal:** if a YAML field *key* is in German, or a rendered page heading is in English (without a deliberate bilingual context), something is wrong.
-
-### 1.6 Build output is assembled, not generated twice
-
-The deployment pipeline produces exactly one directory (`dist/`) that is uploaded to GitHub Pages. VitePress owns the root of `dist/`. The arc42 static site is built separately and placed under `dist/architecture/` before the single Pages upload. No content is built twice; no build step overwrites output from another.
-
-**Defect signal:** if the GitHub Actions deploy workflow uploads more than one artifact to GitHub Pages, or if `dist/` is cleared after arc42 has written to `dist/architecture/`, something is wrong.
-
-### 1.7 The platform is forkable at zero cost
-
-No file in the repository may reference any account-specific secret, username, or URL that would break after a fork without editing source code. The GitHub Pages URL in config is derived from the repository URL, not hard-coded. The only hard-coded value is the base path `/edugo/` — which is the repository name, not an account name.
-
-**Defect signal:** if a fork of this repository must change any file other than a deployment configuration file to produce a working site, something is wrong.
-
